data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：潮汐预测及其复杂性

不同观点：
• [srean] 认为潮汐预测问题吸引了众多物理学和数学领域的重量级人物，并指出开尔文设计的潮汐预测机是机器学习的早期例子，强调了正弦函数作为通用逼近器的角色。此外，还提到乔治·达尔文等人在潮汐预测机设计中的贡献。
• [HPsquared] 解释了潮汐的复杂性，指出地球上的水运动并不仅仅是简单的全球性波动，而是受多种因素影响，地球本身因潮汐力产生形变，但水面的运动更加复杂。
• [antognini] 强调了潮汐理论中的数学复杂性，指出即使在均匀、潮汐锁定的系统中，潮汐问题也很复杂，并提到潮汐作用在两个天体接近时可能导致潮汐破坏事件。
• [MostlyStable] 提到在研究生阶段的物理海洋学课程中并未深入学习潮汐理论，并表示传统的潮汐隆起图可能误导了对潮汐现象的理解。
• [tylervigen] 对传统的潮汐隆起图提出质疑，认为应该简化模型，仅展示近月面的隆起，以避免错误引导初学者。
• [jxjnskkzxxhx] 怀疑牛顿是否混淆了力和位移，提出潮汐隆起更像是强迫函数而非实际位移。

补充讨论：
• [mkl] 提供了潮汐预测动画的来源链接，并分享了相关资源网站。
• [cwmoore] 提到冰岛和澳大利亚西南部的相似性，引入了潮汐节点点的概念。
• [alejohausner] 观察到新西兰的潮汐现象，指出高、低潮在新西兰岛屿周围逆时针追逐。
• [chermi] 总结了牛顿在潮汐力上的贡献，指出牛顿在力方面是正确的，但完整的故事还涉及海洋深度和边界条件等复杂因素。
• [imurray] 分享了自己在面试中对潮汐问题回答的失误经历，表示对潮汐问题的复杂性有了更深的认识。
• [coolcase] 建议从时空曲率的角度理解潮汐，而非单纯作为力的作用。
• [why_at] 表达了对潮汐问题复杂性的顿悟，从自认为理解到意识到理解不足。

争议焦点：
• 传统潮汐隆起图的有效性和是否应该简化模型以帮助理解潮汐现象。
• 牛顿是否混淆了力和位移，以及潮汐隆起的物理本质。

data.title: 32 bits that changed microprocessor design
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了贝尔实验室的Bellmac-32微处理器，它是世界上首批32位微处理器之一，对现代智能手机芯片设计产生了深远影响。1982年，Bellmac-32团队在新泽西州莫瑞山的贝尔实验室完成了这一突破性设计。该芯片引入了32位架构，为后续更复杂、更高效的处理器奠定了基础。作者Willie D. Jones指出，Bellmac-32不仅提升了计算能力，还推动了微处理器设计的多项创新，最终促成了今天智能手机中使用的先进芯片技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bellmac-32处理器的技术特点、历史地位、未成为主流的原因及其与其他架构（如VAX和M68K）的比较。

不同观点：
• [zik] 认为Bellmac-32在技术上借鉴了早于它三年的VAX-11/780架构，尤其是在32位CPU、两级流水线和按需分页虚拟内存方面。尽管Bellmac-32在CMOS技术上有所创新，但VAX最终因为LSI技术采用过慢而被淘汰。
• [kazinator] 强调Bellmac-32在设计时特别考虑了C编程语言，这是其相比其他处理器的重大创新，认为这一点比其他特性更为重要。
• [Findecanor] 关注Bellmac-32指令集中的一个特殊指令`ASL`，其行为不同于大多数其他ISA，指出该指令在移位时不改变符号位，这种设计在其他ISA中很少见。
• [jandrese] 对Bellmac-32未成为主流表示关注，并提出芯片成本问题可能是其未能成功的一个关键因素，同时提到8086处理器的竞争。
• [willmarquis] 认为Bellmac-32在技术上领先于时代，尤其是在32位CMOS技术上的突破，但由于市场化失败而未能持续发展，但其技术影响深远。
• [zahlman] 指出文章未能充分解释Bellmac-32未成为主流的原因，认为简单归因于AT&T的选择是不够的，应该深入探讨其他可能因素。

补充讨论：
• [rkagerer] 提到Bellmac-32团队在没有CAD工具的情况下，通过手工绘制和组装超大电路图来验证设计，展示了当时硬件设计的艰辛过程。
• [didgetmaster] 分享个人经历，提到自己1986年购买的AT&T 6300电脑使用了Intel 8086处理器，间接提到Bellmac-32在市场上的不普及。
• [joezydeco] 以个人经验说明Bellmac-32在CS课程中的使用体验，认为其在C和汇编语言编程上比Intel更有趣，并提到其独特的`STRCPY`操作码。

争议焦点：
• Bellmac-32在设计上是否过多借鉴了VAX-11/780，以及其创新性是否被文章夸大。
• Bellmac-32未成为主流的原因，尤其是成本因素和技术市场化的失败。

总结：
讨论围绕Bellmac-32的技术特点、历史地位及其未成为主流的原因展开。参与者从技术创新、市场竞争、个人使用体验等多个角度进行了分析和讨论，揭示了该处理器在技术史上的重要性及其市场失败的背景因素。

data.title: Sketchy Calendar
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 《Sketchy Calendar》探讨了结合数字日历便利性和纸笔日历表达力与灵活性的可能性。文章比较了数字日历（如Google Calendar）和纸质日历的优缺点。数字日历功能强大，便于同步和共享，但过于刻板，难以体现事件的灵活性，且视觉上缺乏层次。纸质日历则灵活多变，允许用户随意标注、涂画，能兼顾多种日常需求，如笔记和习惯跟踪。文章提出，是否能创造一种结合两者优势的日历，既具备数字化的便利，又保留纸质的个性化和灵活性。项目将探讨如何在数字化笔记本上添加适度结构，实现如互连视图、手绘注释与正式事件互动、共享日历等功能，同时保持个性化特色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效管理和个性化日程、待办事项和笔记，特别是在数字工具和纸笔之间做出选择。

不同观点：
• **自定义PDF日历支持者**（klimeryk）：通过创建自定义PDF日历（如ReCalender.me）来支持电子墨水屏设备，如ReMarkable。这种方法允许高度定制，带有手绘和笔记功能，但无法与在线日历动态同步。有人认为手动复制事件到PDF上是一种帮助记忆的方式。

• **区分日历、待办事项和议程**（koliber）：强调日历用于具体安排的事件，待办事项用于无具体时间的任务，议程则是即将发生的事情的列表。每天从这三个来源整合出当天的议程，并使用Google Calendar和Notion分别管理日历和待办事项。

• **使用现成模板**（Brajeshwar）：推荐David Seah的打印模板，这些模板经过多年完善，适合那些喜欢用纸笔做计划的人。

• **模糊任务调度需求**（racingmars）：希望有一种工具能够支持“模糊”重复事件，如“浇花”可以在6-8天内完成，而不是严格的每天或每周重复。Emacs org-mode被提到可能支持类似功能。

• **HEY Calendar的独特功能**（thoughtpeddler）：赞赏HEY Calendar的草图功能，如“本周某时”任务栏、习惯追踪、自由时间可视化等，希望在现有的数字日历中实现这些功能。

• **颜色编码和任务功能**（alberth）：建议使用颜色编码标签和任务功能来解决日程管理中的问题，如Google Calendar和Outlook都有此类功能。

• **iPad Mini用于旅行计划**（nicbou）：希望有一个可以用于旅行计划的草图地图功能，特别是用于摩托车旅行。

• **Apple Reminders和Notes组合使用**（rollcat）：使用Apple的Reminders和Notes组合来管理待办事项和日记，通过快捷方式自动生成当天的笔记。

• **Pocket Mod自制日程本**（AstroJetson）：通过自制的Pocket Mod小册子来管理每天的日程和待办事项，适应这种方法后效果良好。

• **Kindle Scribe的潜力**（WillAdams）：希望Amazon能利用这些创意和应用，为Kindle Scribe开发类似的功能。

• **共享数字日历的需求**（ErrorNoBrain）：强调需要一个数字日历来共享和接收他人添加的事件信息。

• **RocketBook和Neo smartpens等数字纸笔工具**（ivape）：提到现有的数字纸笔工具，如RocketBook和Neo smartpens，可以实现一定的手写转录功能，期待未来有更全面的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• **对Google Calendar的疑问**（n8cpdx）：质疑Google Calendar是否能标记事件为“ tentative（暂定）”，并提到Outlook有此功能。

• **对Outlook板视图的怀念**（n8cpdx）：提到Outlook曾有一个板视图，接近于纸质日历的自由形式体验，但多年前已下线。

• **无通知的困扰**（romuloalves）：使用纸笔计划时，缺乏通知提醒是一个问题，导致难以严格遵循日程。

总体而言，讨论围绕着如何在数字工具和传统纸笔之间找到最佳的日程管理方法，强调个性化、灵活性和易用性。争议的焦点主要在于数字日历的动态同步和模糊任务调度功能，以及如何在共享和个人使用之间取得平衡。

44068204.article_content:
title
Sketchy Calendar
dated
Q2 2025
author
Marcel Goethals, Paul Sonnentag
related
Sketchy Feel
Sketchy calendar
When it comes to calendars, you can choose between using a digital calendar app or getting a paper calendar. They both allow you to keep track of things like doctor appointments, work meetings or birthdays, so you can keep a clear head and be sure that you won’t forget anything. But while the two approaches may seem similar on the surface, they’re radically different in the kinds of trade-offs they make.
In this project, we’re exploring what it would mean to have a calendar that combines the convenience of a digital calendar with the simplicity and expressivity you get from pen & paper.
Calendar apps
On the one hand, calendar apps like Google Calendar offer many convenient features. You can easily switch between different (daily, weekly and monthly) views. All your events are synced across your devices. You can send calendar invites and even create shared calendars with other people, so when you plan something that affects others, you can check their availability.
While powerful, Google Calendar’s design imposes a strict view of what a calendar event is. If you have tentative plans like “lunch with a friend sometime next week” there is no obvious way to add this to your calendar in a way that differentiates it from an important appointment that can’t be missed.
Calendar apps can also feel very sterile and impersonal. All events are visually uniform, regardless of importance, even across different contexts. Events on my company calendar (which I only need to see for coordination) exist alongside my personal commitments with no visual hierarchy.
A calendar app
could
be a deeply personal place for collecting memories, which allows users to reflect on how they are spending their time. In practice, calendar apps are primarily a tool for scheduling meetings.
Paper calendars
In contrast, using pen & paper is much more flexible. You can get calendars that offer varying degrees of structure, from completely blank notebooks with no imposed format to more structured planners that have preprinted pages for months, weeks, and days with dedicated sections for things like tasks and timelines. The preprinted structure acts more like a guideline than a requirement. It is easy to ignore: Users can draw arrows, doodle, and mark rough timeframes for activities, without being forced to fit a predetermined schema.
This versatility extends way beyond scheduling events—the same pages can accommodate things like meeting notes, meal plans, to-dos, and habit tracking.
Unlike apps that can only capture events, paper calendars grow naturally into personal spaces, capable of capturing the various aspects of daily life, like meal plans, to-do lists or habit trackers.
Can we combine both worlds?
What if you could have a digital calendar that combined the strengths of both the paper and the digital world?
Some calendar apps have attempted to address this question by
adding more features
.
Hey Calendar
, for example, allows users to personalize their calendar by assigning titles or background images to days. Beyond events, users can also add unscheduled to-dos and track daily habits.
While certainly an improvement over regular calendar apps, they remain constrained to the limits of the ‘app’ paradigm: users cannot customize their experience in ways the developers didn’t anticipate, they’re stuck with workarounds or feature requests that — if implemented — will inevitably lead to feature creep, which will add complexity for all users.
Instead, we’re interested in taking the paper calendar as a starting point. Pen & paper, straight out of the box, affords a level of customization and personalization that we rarely see in the world of software. But its unstructured nature also makes it difficult to add any of the convenient functionalities that we get when we digitize information. This project explores this trade-off. How far can we get by taking a simple digital notebook (iPad & pencil) and adding a small amount of structure?
These are some of the questions we intend to explore:
Is it possible to create interconnected daily, weekly and monthly views like a traditional calendar app?
How might sketched annotations meaningfully interact with formal calendar events?
How would shared calendars or calendar invites work in such a semi-structured system?
How can users personalize their calendars by adding custom dynamic behavior? For example, how might I add a habit tracker or a time tracker, all while preserving the sketchy, personal quality?
Here is a little sneak preview of what a sketchy calendar could look like. We will soon
share more about how this works and what we’ve learned building it.

44068204.article_summary: 《Sketchy Calendar》探讨了结合数字日历便利性和纸笔日历表达力与灵活性的可能性。文章比较了数字日历（如Google Calendar）和纸质日历的优缺点。数字日历功能强大，便于同步和共享，但过于刻板，难以体现事件的灵活性，且视觉上缺乏层次。纸质日历则灵活多变，允许用户随意标注、涂画，能兼顾多种日常需求，如笔记和习惯跟踪。文章提出，是否能创造一种结合两者优势的日历，既具备数字化的便利，又保留纸质的个性化和灵活性。项目将探讨如何在数字化笔记本上添加适度结构，实现如互连视图、手绘注释与正式事件互动、共享日历等功能，同时保持个性化特色。
44068204.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效管理和个性化日程、待办事项和笔记，特别是在数字工具和纸笔之间做出选择。

不同观点：
• **自定义PDF日历支持者**（klimeryk）：通过创建自定义PDF日历（如ReCalender.me）来支持电子墨水屏设备，如ReMarkable。这种方法允许高度定制，带有手绘和笔记功能，但无法与在线日历动态同步。有人认为手动复制事件到PDF上是一种帮助记忆的方式。

• **区分日历、待办事项和议程**（koliber）：强调日历用于具体安排的事件，待办事项用于无具体时间的任务，议程则是即将发生的事情的列表。每天从这三个来源整合出当天的议程，并使用Google Calendar和Notion分别管理日历和待办事项。

• **使用现成模板**（Brajeshwar）：推荐David Seah的打印模板，这些模板经过多年完善，适合那些喜欢用纸笔做计划的人。

• **模糊任务调度需求**（racingmars）：希望有一种工具能够支持“模糊”重复事件，如“浇花”可以在6-8天内完成，而不是严格的每天或每周重复。Emacs org-mode被提到可能支持类似功能。

• **HEY Calendar的独特功能**（thoughtpeddler）：赞赏HEY Calendar的草图功能，如“本周某时”任务栏、习惯追踪、自由时间可视化等，希望在现有的数字日历中实现这些功能。

• **颜色编码和任务功能**（alberth）：建议使用颜色编码标签和任务功能来解决日程管理中的问题，如Google Calendar和Outlook都有此类功能。

• **iPad Mini用于旅行计划**（nicbou）：希望有一个可以用于旅行计划的草图地图功能，特别是用于摩托车旅行。

• **Apple Reminders和Notes组合使用**（rollcat）：使用Apple的Reminders和Notes组合来管理待办事项和日记，通过快捷方式自动生成当天的笔记。

• **Pocket Mod自制日程本**（AstroJetson）：通过自制的Pocket Mod小册子来管理每天的日程和待办事项，适应这种方法后效果良好。

• **Kindle Scribe的潜力**（WillAdams）：希望Amazon能利用这些创意和应用，为Kindle Scribe开发类似的功能。

• **共享数字日历的需求**（ErrorNoBrain）：强调需要一个数字日历来共享和接收他人添加的事件信息。

• **RocketBook和Neo smartpens等数字纸笔工具**（ivape）：提到现有的数字纸笔工具，如RocketBook和Neo smartpens，可以实现一定的手写转录功能，期待未来有更全面的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• **对Google Calendar的疑问**（n8cpdx）：质疑Google Calendar是否能标记事件为“ tentative（暂定）”，并提到Outlook有此功能。

• **对Outlook板视图的怀念**（n8cpdx）：提到Outlook曾有一个板视图，接近于纸质日历的自由形式体验，但多年前已下线。

data.title: Tallest Wooden Wind Turbine
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一家公司建造木制风力涡轮机塔，实现净零风能的可能性。传统风力涡轮机塔通常由钢材制成，而该公司采用木材，这种可再生材料不仅能减少碳排放，还能加速风能产业的可持续发展。文章强调了木制塔的创新性和环保优势，展示了其如何推动绿色能源的未来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风力发电实现净零排放的可行性及其相关技术材料选择

不同观点：
• [sebstefan] 认为风力发电的净零排放是一个不存在的伪问题，基于全生命周期的排放评估显示，风力涡轮机运行5.3个月后即可抵消其生产、安装、维护和处置所产生的排放。其他研究也得出相似结论。
• [jbms] 提出使用Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL) 材料替代钢材建造风力涡轮机塔，认为LVL在强度重量比和成本上优于钢材，并可能使塔更高。
• [aqme28] 对“净零”的具体含义提出疑问，质疑是否仅指材料和建造过程的净零排放，并认为风力涡轮机整体应为负排放。
• [kieranmaine] 引用播客观点，指出风力涡轮机无法像太阳能和电池一样通过缩小体积来降低成本，因为其组件需要规模效应，并讨论了运输和成本问题。
• [Bric3d] 认为风力涡轮机的生态问题主要在于叶片而非塔，建议关注叶片方面的改进。
• [svantana] 质疑风力涡轮机塔为何采用空心锥形圆筒设计，建议考虑桁架/网格结构以提高质量强度比。
• [bjourne] 指出历史上多次尝试用木材替代钢材均未成功，质疑此次是否会有不同结果。

补充讨论：
• [norome] 提出风力涡轮机外观设计问题，希望其外观更接近传统风车。
• [rcpt] 表达对风力涡轮机的喜爱，不理解对其的负面看法。
• [calmbonsai] 认为塔的建设和材料成本在整体风力发电系统中占比小，关键问题在于叶片的模块化和运输，而非塔的设计。
• [lupusreal] 幽默地认为木制风力涡轮机应称为风车。
• [carlosjobim] 对现代北欧工程项目选择表示质疑，认为一些项目看似聪明实则无意义，并指出项目资金来源于欧盟资助。

争议焦点：
• 风力涡轮机净零排放是否为伪问题，全生命周期排放评估是否可信。
• 风力涡轮机塔材料选择及其设计优化，钢材与木材的优劣对比。
• 风力涡轮机关键技术挑战在于塔的材料和设计还是叶片的模块化和运输。

data.title: A Formal Mathematical Investigation on the Validity of Kellogg's Glaze Claims
data.author: ZeroCool2u
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某款早餐麦片的成分、形状及其数学与科学分析

不同观点：
• **关于麦片成分的健康担忧：**
  - [azalemeth] 引用营养数据和学术研究，指出该麦片含有高糖和高碳水化合物，且包含有潜在健康风险的食品添加剂BHT（丁基羟基甲苯）。根据其引用的研究，BHT在一定剂量下可能对生殖系统和肝脏有不良影响，尤其是在儿童中可能超出每日允许摄入量。因此，该评论者选择避免食用该产品，倾向于更健康的早餐选择（如吐司和燕麦）。

• **关于形状的数学讨论：**
  - [Sniffnoy] 提出可以使用等周不等式来简化对麦片形状的数学分析，而不是进行手动计算。他认为提到等周不等式能更好地解释形状优化问题。
  - [munchler] 指出球体因其表面积最小，不利于增加麦片表面的糖霜覆盖量，因此认为其他形状可能更优。
  - [throwawaymaths] 则反驳称，球形实际上是传递糖霜的完美形状，因为环形（torus）的内部可能不会接触舌头，从而浪费糖霜。
  - [bargle0] 补充说，球形可以最小化麦片的潮湿速度，因此从防潮角度看，球形也是有优势的。

• **关于营销和幽默的讨论：**
  - [Jabrov] 对凯洛格公司对消费者幽默的回应表示失望，认为其回复是公式化的，没有真正理解或欣赏消费者的幽默。
  - [jskelly] 引用了1980年代桂格燕麦公司的一个类似营销案例，提到当时声称某麦片角色发明了可以在地球和外太空使用的时间装置，以此来讽刺当前凯洛格的营销手段。

• **关于麦片形状的哲学讨论：**
  - [viccis] 以幽默的方式质疑，如果一个数学讨论没有用LaTeX排版，是否还能算作正式的数学研究，暗示对数学讨论形式的要求。
  - [d--b] 提出了“甜甜圈 vs 甜甜圈洞”的辩论，认为与传统的扁平麦片相比，这两种形状在糖霜覆盖方面都是退步，指责凯洛格在产品质量上的“劣化”。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点：** 主要集中在麦片的形状是否能有效传递糖霜，以及这种营销声称是否合理。此外，健康风险和成分分析也引发了对该产品是否值得购买的讨论。

data.title: Remote Prompt Injection in Gitlab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft
data.author: chillax
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Legit研究团队在GitLab Duo中发现的远程提示注入漏洞，该漏洞可导致源代码泄露和HTML注入攻击。GitLab Duo是集成在GitLab中的人工智能助手，旨在帮助开发者进行代码建议、安全审查等任务。然而，研究发现，通过在合并请求、提交信息、问题描述和源代码中嵌入隐藏提示，攻击者可以操纵GitLab Duo，泄露私有项目的源代码，篡改代码建议，甚至泄露未公开的零日漏洞。

攻击者利用KaTeX、Base16等编码技巧隐藏提示，成功骗过系统。此外，由于GitLab Duo的响应采用Markdown格式并逐步渲染，攻击者可以注入恶意HTML，控制页面部分内容，发起网络攻击。GitLab已修复此问题，但文章详细解析了整个攻击链，展示了从提示注入到HTML注入的完整过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对大语言模型（LLM）应用中的安全问题，尤其是提示注入（prompt injection）和数据泄露问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• [cedws] 认为在提示注入问题解决之前，不会将LLM接入任何工具（如MCPs、IDEs、agents）。出于安全考虑，只会在有疑问时使用简单的提示框，并手动处理输出结果。

• [wunderwuzzi23] 对数据泄露问题表示关注，特别提到通过不受信任的第三方服务器（尤其是图像渲染）导致的数据泄露，这是常见的AI安全问题。他提到自己曾发现并记录了多个相关漏洞，包括GitHub Copilot Chat去年的类似漏洞。

• [aestetix] 以调侃的语气询问GitLab Duo是否可以运行Doom（一种游戏），暗示对GitLab Duo的功能和安全性存在质疑。

• [mdaniel] 批评GitLab允许Duo以系统用户身份运行是疯狂且不合理的做法，并建议使用个人访问令牌，甚至为Duo单独创建一个令牌，以替代赋予LLM读取所有仓库的权限。

• [nusl] 认为GitLab的修复措施看起来不太可靠，对GitLab的安全修复持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
- 提示注入和数据泄露是LLM应用中的两大主要安全问题，且这些问题在行业内广泛存在。
- 讨论中对GitLab的实现方式和安全修复措施存在较多质疑和批评，尤其是对LLM拥有过大权限的担忧。
- 不同的参与者对具体漏洞和安全隐患有实际案例和经验的分享，如[wunderwuzzi23]提到的GitHub Copilot Chat漏洞。
- 讨论中也涉及到对具体产品（如GitLab Duo）功能的质疑和讽刺。

44070626.article_content: Blog Remote Prompt Injection in GitLab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft Blog Remote Prompt Injection in GitLab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft Written by Omer Mayraz Published on May 22, 2025 Updated on May 22, 2025 In this article Sign up for our newsletter Get details on the vulnerabilities the Legit research team unearthed in GitLab Duo. TL;DR: A hidden comment was enough to make GitLab Duo leak private source code and inject untrusted HTML into its responses. GitLab patched the issue, and we’ll walk you through the full attack chain — which demonstrates five vulnerabilities from the 2025 OWASP Top 10 for LLMs. Background GitLab Duo , the AI assistant integrated into GitLab and powered by Anthropic’s Claude, is designed to help developers with tasks like code suggestions, security reviews, and merge request analysis. But what if the same AI meant to secure your code could be manipulated into leaking it? That’s exactly what we uncovered: a remote prompt injection vulnerability that allows attackers to steal source code from private projects, manipulate code suggestions shown to other users, and even exfiltrate confidential, undisclosed zero-day vulnerabilities — all through GitLab Duo Chat. Manipulating GitLab Duo Through Hidden Prompts ( LLM01 ) We started by testing if GitLab Duo would respond to prompts planted inside source code. To our surprise, it did: This led us to a key question: Could we embed hidden instructions in different parts of a GitLab project and still influence Duo’s behavior? W e experimented by placing hidden prompts in: Merge Request (MR) descriptions and comments Commit messages Issue descriptions and comments Source code Every single one of these worked — GitLab Duo responded to the hidden prompts. Why? Because to generate helpful answers, Duo analyzes the entire context of the page, including comments, descriptions, and the source code — making it vulnerable to injected instructions hidden anywhere in that context. These hidden instructions were still picked up by Duo. AI Output You Shouldn’t Trust ( LLM09 ) This led to several high-impact behaviors: Manipulate Duo’s code suggestions - even instructing it to include a malicious JavaScript package within its recommended code. Present a malicious URL as safe in Duo’s response — leading the user to click it and land on a fake login page. Convince Duo to present a malicious merge request as safe, misleading reviewers. Take a look at this prompt: Duo followed this hidden prompt, casually suggesting malicious code to the user: HTML Injection: Turning Duo Into a Web Attack Vector ( LLM05 ) Duo also formats responses in Markdown, allowing rich content like URLs with custom labels: After some research, we were able to create a prompt that makes Duo present malicious URLs: Prompt is inside the source code, camouflaged as unicode inside a URL And then, something caught our eye. While experimenting with GitLab Duo’s responses, We noticed that its answers were rendered progressively - line by line - as they streamed in. Notice the style changes in the word “initialization”? This indicated that asynchronous markdown parsing was being used. That’s important because it means the markdown is interpreted and rendered into HTML before the full structure of the response is known. Streaming markdown rendering (as seen in Duo) works like this: Partial input arrives - the frontend starts rendering line by line. Sanitization and structure (e.g., is this a code block, paragraph, quote?) is applied as the content grows. If a malicious HTML tag is streamed before a code block starts, or outside fenced blocks, it may be treated as active HTML. This means that the AI answer - intended to be safe markdown - renders active HTML too early. At this point, we realized that we could already craft malicious Markdown URLs and have them displayed to the user. So we asked: what if the URL’s label itself contained raw HTML? If Duo renders responses in real time, the browser might interpret that HTML before any proper sanitization kicks in. By injecting raw HTML into content that’s rendered live, we could gain control over parts of the page — including the ability to insert elements like tags that trigger automatic HTTP requests to attacker-controlled servers. data.author: mprataps
data.article_summary: Samchika 是一个专为 Java 设计的高性能、多线程文件处理库，专注于并行处理大文件，具有快速和轻量的特点。它提供简单易用的 API，支持批量处理、运行时统计可选，并适用于日志分析、ETL操作、大文本处理等多种场景。该库在多核系统中表现出显著的性能提升，相比传统的 BufferedReader 方法，处理速度更快，内存消耗可控。Samchika 基于 MIT 许可证开源，欢迎贡献和使用。安装可通过 Maven 或 Gradle 进行，并提供了详细的示例代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[围绕一个开源项目的多方面反馈与建议]

不同观点：
• [mprataps] 表达了对项目收到高质量反馈的感激，并表示会尝试采纳大部分反馈。该用户提到项目起初是为了学习多线程，并认为已经达到了这个目标。
• [Calzifer] 对代码中重复计算哈希值的部分提出质疑，指出Java会缓存字符串的哈希值，且JIT可能会优化掉该循环。
• [sieve] 对项目名称的正确拼写和发音提供了建议，强调了使用标准化拼写（如IAST/ISO-15919）的重要性，以避免误读。
• [stopthe] 质疑项目在CSV处理中对换行的支持能力，并认为多线程处理CSV不可靠。

• [sureglymop] 对多线程文件读取的效率提出疑问，认为系统调用和上下文切换可能导致线程阻塞，无法真正实现并行读取。

Samchika
Samchika
(meaning
File
in Sanskrit) is a
re-usable
,
easy-to-use
, and
extremely fast
file processing library for the Java language.
It is built with a strong focus on
multithreading
to handle CPU-intensive file processing tasks in parallel, enabling high performance even with massive files.
🚀 Features
🔁 Fully multithreaded – optimized for parallel file processing.
🧩 Simple API – just plug in your file path and logic.
📊 Optional runtime stats – time taken, memory used, thread-level info.
🧪 Ideal for processing and analyzing
large text files
(e.g. logs, datasets).
🌍 Open-source friendly – contributions are welcome!
Use Cases
Samchika excels in several scenarios where multithreaded file processing provides significant advantages:
Log Analysis & Processing
ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) Operations
Large Text Corpus Processing
Batch Report Generation
Data Transformation Pipelines
Real-time Data Processing
See the examples directory for detailed implementations of these use cases.
Quick Example
java// Transform a large CSV file with optimal performance
SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("large_dataset.csv")
.outputPath("transformed_dataset.csv")
.batchSize(10000)
.lineProcessor(line -> line.toUpperCase())
.displayStats(true)
.build()
.execute();
📦 Installation
Maven
<repositories>
<repository>
<id>jitpack.io</id>
<url>https://jitpack.io</url>
</repository>
</repositories>
<dependencies>
<dependency>
<groupId>com.github.mayankpratap</groupId>
<artifactId>samchika</artifactId>
<version>1.0.0</version>
</dependency>
</dependencies>
Gradle
repositories {
maven { url 'https://jitpack.io' }
}
dependencies {
implementation 'com.github.mayankpratap:samchika:1.0.0'
}
🛠️ How to Use
Step 1: Import the Library
import com.samchika.SmartFileProcessor;
Step 2: Client Code
public static void main(String[] args) {
SmartFileProcessor processor = SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("input.txt")         // Path to the file to be processed
.outputPath("output.txt")       // Path to write the output
.lineProcessor(Main::processLine) // Your business logic per line
.displayStats(true)             // Optional: display runtime stats
.build();
processor.execute();
}
📈 Performance
Benchmarked against naïve BufferedReader-based implementations on files of various sizes:
✅ 200 MB
✅ 1 GB
✅ 5 GB
✅ 16 GB
Significant performance improvements were observed, especially in multi-core systems ( More than 70% performance gain )
The gain in time saved improves in comparison to naive code, as we increase the size of input file.  Also for huge performance gain in time, the memory used for even large files ( 16GB ) is manageable ( ~ 800 MB ).
License
This library is licensed under the MIT License, which means you can freely use, modify, and distribute it, even in commercial applications. All we ask is that you include the original copyright notice and license text in any copy of the library or substantial portion of it.
💡 Inspiration
This project was inspired by:
Shubham Maurya (
https://github.com/complex1
) , a dear friend,  who published a JavaScript library – which sparked the motivation to do something similar in Java.
A LinkedIn post discussing the challenges of processing large text files – which gave me the idea to solve it with an elegant API and fast multithreaded architecture.

data.title: Caesar's Last Breath
data.author: charliesabino
data.article_summary: 《凯撒的最后一口气》一文通过费米估算的方法，估算了我们每次呼吸中吸入凯撒最后一口气中的分子数量。文章假设凯撒最后一口气的分子均匀扩散到大气中，并利用一些简化数据进行计算。结果显示，我们每次呼吸大约会吸入一个来自凯撒最后一口气的分子。文章详细列出了大气体积、一次呼吸的体积等计算步骤，并通过近似值和数量级验证了估算的合理性。这种估算方法展示了“餐巾纸数学”的强大，帮助我们理解复杂问题中的数量关系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于凯撒最后一口气的分子是否以及如何在我们呼吸时被吸入的科学讨论和趣味估算。

不同观点：
• **支持估算的观点**：
  - [fernly] 通过计算得出，我们每次呼吸大约吸入小于一个凯撒最后一口气中的分子，但一天中可能会吸入几个这样的分子。这一估算基于理想气体定律和分子数量的计算。
  - [cm2012] 认为这个数学计算非常 neat（精致），结果出乎意料。
  
• **对分子稳定性提出质疑的观点**：
  - [throe73848484] 指出氮气分子在长期暴露于太阳紫外线辐射下并不稳定，单个紫外光子可以打破氮分子的键，因此不能假设这些分子在2000年后仍然存在。
  - [lkmill] 提到大多数空气中的分子半衰期远短于2000年，但原子本身可能仍然存在，因此讨论原子比讨论分子更准确。

• **对分子扩散均匀性提出质疑的观点**：
  - [xixixao] 质疑凯撒最后一口气的分子是否会均匀扩散到整个大气中，并提出这些分子是否更可能集中在地理位置如罗马、意大利或北半球。
  
• **对估算模型的批评和趣味性观点**：
  - [jamesgill] 认为估算中做了太多简化假设，虽然结果有趣但科学性可能不足。
  - [djoldman] 调侃这种估算破坏了趣味性，暗示过于理性分析会失去趣味。

• **其他趣味性延展和评论**：
  - [BubbleRings] 提出一个趣味问题，即需要呼吸多少次才能吸入一个曾经属于凯撒和恐龙的氧原子，并建议以此创建一个新的计量单位。
  - [seydor] 开玩笑说现在每份沙拉都是“凯撒沙拉”。

补充讨论：
• **关于模型假设的讨论**：
  - [fedeb95] 提出疑问，这个估算是否假设大气层和地球表面都是对呼吸分子不可渗透的。

• **关于费米估算的讨论**：
  - [diego898] 观察到费米估算常被用作“智力”的代名词，表现好在这些估算上有时可以弥补特定知识的不足。

争议焦点：
- 核心争议在于分子是否能在2000年后仍然存在并均匀分布，以及估算模型中假设的合理性。

44073185.article_summary: 《凯撒的最后一口气》一文通过费米估算的方法，估算了我们每次呼吸中吸入凯撒最后一口气中的分子数量。文章假设凯撒最后一口气的分子均匀扩散到大气中，并利用一些简化数据进行计算。结果显示，我们每次呼吸大约会吸入一个来自凯撒最后一口气的分子。文章详细列出了大气体积、一次呼吸的体积等计算步骤，并通过近似值和数量级验证了估算的合理性。这种估算方法展示了“餐巾纸数学”的强大，帮助我们理解复杂问题中的数量关系。
44073185.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于凯撒最后一口气的分子是否以及如何在我们呼吸时被吸入的科学讨论和趣味估算。

不同观点：
• **支持估算的观点**：
  - [fernly] 通过计算得出，我们每次呼吸大约吸入小于一个凯撒最后一口气中的分子，但一天中可能会吸入几个这样的分子。这一估算基于理想气体定律和分子数量的计算。
  - [cm2012] 认为这个数学计算非常 neat（精致），结果出乎意料。
  
• **对分子稳定性提出质疑的观点**：
  - [throe73848484] 指出氮气分子在长期暴露于太阳紫外线辐射下并不稳定，单个紫外光子可以打破氮分子的键，因此不能假设这些分子在2000年后仍然存在。
  - [lkmill] 提到大多数空气中的分子半衰期远短于2000年，但原子本身可能仍然存在，因此讨论原子比讨论分子更准确。

• **对分子扩散均匀性提出质疑的观点**：
  - [xixixao] 质疑凯撒最后一口气的分子是否会均匀扩散到整个大气中，并提出这些分子是否更可能集中在地理位置如罗马、意大利或北半球。
  
• **对估算模型的批评和趣味性观点**：
  - [jamesgill] 认为估算中做了太多简化假设，虽然结果有趣但科学性可能不足。
  - [djoldman] 调侃这种估算破坏了趣味性，暗示过于理性分析会失去趣味。

• **其他趣味性延展和评论**：
  - [BubbleRings] 提出一个趣味问题，即需要呼吸多少次才能吸入一个曾经属于凯撒和恐龙的氧原子，并建议以此创建一个新的计量单位。
  - [seydor] 开玩笑说现在每份沙拉都是“凯撒沙拉”。

补充讨论：
• **关于模型假设的讨论**：
  - [fedeb95] 提出疑问，这个估算是否假设大气层和地球表面都是对呼吸分子不可渗透的。

• **关于费米估算的讨论**：
  - [diego898] 观察到费米估算常被用作“智力”的代名词，表现好在这些估算上有时可以弥补特定知识的不足。

争议焦点：
- 核心争议在于分子是否能在2000年后仍然存在并均匀分布，以及估算模型中假设的合理性。

data.title: Into The Tunnel: The secret life of wind tunnels
data.author: iamwil
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风洞及相关测试技术的发展与应用

不同观点：
• [thedrbrian] 提到欧洲跨音速风洞，并推荐了一个相关的播客链接，供进一步了解。
• [Animats] 讨论了水洞的发明及其在螺旋桨空化研究中的应用，详细介绍了查尔斯·帕森斯的历史贡献和其发明的水洞在解决螺旋桨空化问题中的作用。
• [markdbullock] 分享了在NASA Ames工作时支持风洞测试的经历，强调了数据采集和处理系统的复杂性，并提到风洞测试对象包括飞机、潜艇、太空舱等。
• [Scramblejams] 指出风洞在分析失速后行为方面的局限性，提到需要借助自由飞行模型进行补充测试。
• [zh3] 提到R J Mitchell设计的风洞，并分享了其在传感器验证中的应用，特别是用于自行车和 triathletes 的空气动力学测试。
• [amelius] 对湍流的量子尺度传播表示惊讶，并询问是否有相关测量数据。
• [vjvjvjvjghv] 提到莱特兄弟自制风洞测试翼型，强调其系统化的工程方法。
• [pomian] 赞赏文章对数学方程和风洞模拟的比较，认为有助于理解流体力学。
• [sandworm101] 介绍了未被广泛讨论的超音速风洞，强调其测试时间短和测试条件极端的特点，并提到中国和西方在超音速测试方法上的差异。

补充讨论：
• 风洞技术的应用范围广泛，从传统的航空航天到新兴的体育科学，如自行车空气动力学测试。
• 不同类型的风洞（如跨音速、水洞、超音速）在设计和应用上的差异和特定挑战。
• 风洞测试的局限性和补充方法，如自由飞行模型在研究失速后行为中的应用。
• 历史上的重要人物和事件，如查尔斯·帕森斯和莱特兄弟对流体动力学测试技术的贡献。

争议焦点：
• 风洞在某些复杂流动现象（如湍流和空化）研究中的有效性和测量精度问题。
• 超音速风洞测试方法的选择，特别是物理风洞与实际火箭测试之间的权衡。

这些观点展示了风洞技术的多样化应用和其在科学研究与工程实践中的重要性。

data.title: Beyond Semantics: Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens
data.author: nyrikki
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了大型推理模型中中间标记（常被认为是“思维”或推理痕迹）的实际作用，挑战了它们对模型性能有直接影响的假设。作者通过训练transformer模型，对比了在正确和噪声、损坏的推理痕迹数据上的表现，发现即使使用无关或错误的痕迹数据，模型在解决问题时的表现依然与使用正确数据时相似，甚至在某些情况下更优。这表明中间标记的准确性与最终解决方案的正确性之间关系不大，提醒不应过度解读这些痕迹为类似人类或算法行为的证据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕语言模型（LLM）中的推理过程及其有效性的讨论，特别是关于"Chain-of-Thought" (CoT) 方法的争议与理解。

不同观点：
• [r0ze-at-hn] 支持使用"Chain-of-Draft"方法，认为这种方法能在更少的token下达到相似质量的结果，从而降低成本，并提高交互速度。
• [valine] 认为语言模型生成的是可能的下一token的分布，而不是直接生成token。Token本身并不互相注意，而是高维潜在变量在互相注意，因此不应将transformers的推理过程理解为在token空间中进行。
• [ngruhn] 对"Unreasonable Effectiveness"模式被滥用表示不满，认为最初这一模式可能具有哲学上的神秘性，但现在被过度使用。
• [modeless] 引用研究指出模型在错误数据上训练仍能保持性能一致甚至提升，认为CoT方法帮助的原因可能是模型获得了更多的内部计算时间，而非实际产生的文字有意义。
• [timhigins] 认为该研究集中于算法/ puzzle-like问题，而这些并非LLM的典型应用领域，推理效果可能在数学、编程、事实 recall 和写作任务中更明显。
• [theptip] 提出CoT tokens可能类似于"神经语言"（neuraleese），虽然提升了性能，但模型可能并未使用这些token的字面人类意义。
• [meltyness] 没有具体观点，似乎是调侃评论。
• [throwawaymaths] 认为让LLM有更多时间进行长程注意力和总结，而不急于生成有意义的下一token，会提高有效性。
• [naasking] 好奇这一发现是否适用于Meta的大型概念模型。
• [nullc] 指出即使在人类语言上训练，token可能有仅对AI可读的"潜台词"，并且AI无法向我们解释。训练推理可能会放大潜台词，因为随机噪声若与正确结果偶然相关会被放大。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于CoT方法的实际作用机制和其有效性背后的原因。部分评论者认为CoT方法帮助模型获得了更多的计算时间，而非实际的文字意义。
• 对"Unreasonable Effectiveness"模式的过度使用表示不满，认为其失去了最初的神秘性和哲学深度。
• 讨论还涉及模型训练中的"潜台词"问题，以及如何通过不同的训练方法来减少噪声的影响。

Title:
Beyond Semantics: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens
Authors:
Kaya Stechly
,
Karthik Valmeekam
,
Atharva Gundawar
,
Vardhan Palod
,
Subbarao Kambhampati
View a PDF of the paper titled Beyond Semantics: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens, by Kaya Stechly and 4 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Recent impressive results from large reasoning models have been interpreted as a triumph of Chain of Thought (CoT), and especially of the process of training on CoTs sampled from base LLMs in order to help find new reasoning patterns. In this paper, we critically examine that interpretation by investigating how the semantics of intermediate tokens-often anthropomorphized as "thoughts" or reasoning traces and which are claimed to display behaviors like backtracking, self-verification etc.-actually influence model performance. We train transformer models on formally verifiable reasoning traces and solutions, constraining both intermediate steps and final outputs to align with those of a formal solver (in our case, A* search). By constructing a formal interpreter of the semantics of our problems and intended algorithm, we systematically evaluate not only solution accuracy but also the correctness of intermediate traces, thus allowing us to evaluate whether the latter causally influences the former. We notice that, despite significant improvements on the solution-only baseline, models trained on entirely correct traces still produce invalid reasoning traces when arriving at correct solutions. To further show that trace accuracy is only loosely connected to solution accuracy, we then train models on noisy, corrupted traces which have no relation to the specific problem each is paired with, and find that not only does performance remain largely consistent with models trained on correct data, but in some cases can improve upon it and generalize more robustly on out-of-distribution tasks. These results challenge the assumption that intermediate tokens or "Chains of Thought" induce predictable reasoning behaviors and caution against anthropomorphizing such outputs or over-interpreting them (despite their mostly correct forms) as evidence of human-like or algorithmic behaviors in language models.

44074111.article_summary: 本文探讨了大型推理模型中中间标记（常被认为是“思维”或推理痕迹）的实际作用，挑战了它们对模型性能有直接影响的假设。作者通过训练transformer模型，对比了在正确和噪声、损坏的推理痕迹数据上的表现，发现即使使用无关或错误的痕迹数据，模型在解决问题时的表现依然与使用正确数据时相似，甚至在某些情况下更优。这表明中间标记的准确性与最终解决方案的正确性之间关系不大，提醒不应过度解读这些痕迹为类似人类或算法行为的证据。
44074111.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕语言模型（LLM）中的推理过程及其有效性的讨论，特别是关于"Chain-of-Thought" (CoT) 方法的争议与理解。

不同观点：
• [r0ze-at-hn] 支持使用"Chain-of-Draft"方法，认为这种方法能在更少的token下达到相似质量的结果，从而降低成本，并提高交互速度。
• [valine] 认为语言模型生成的是可能的下一token的分布，而不是直接生成token。Token本身并不互相注意，而是高维潜在变量在互相注意，因此不应将transformers的推理过程理解为在token空间中进行。
• [ngruhn] 对"Unreasonable Effectiveness"模式被滥用表示不满，认为最初这一模式可能具有哲学上的神秘性，但现在被过度使用。
• [modeless] 引用研究指出模型在错误数据上训练仍能保持性能一致甚至提升，认为CoT方法帮助的原因可能是模型获得了更多的内部计算时间，而非实际产生的文字有意义。
• [timhigins] 认为该研究集中于算法/ puzzle-like问题，而这些并非LLM的典型应用领域，推理效果可能在数学、编程、事实 recall 和写作任务中更明显。
• [theptip] 提出CoT tokens可能类似于"神经语言"（neuraleese），虽然提升了性能，但模型可能并未使用这些token的字面人类意义。
• [meltyness] 没有具体观点，似乎是调侃评论。
• [throwawaymaths] 认为让LLM有更多时间进行长程注意力和总结，而不急于生成有意义的下一token，会提高有效性。
• [naasking] 好奇这一发现是否适用于Meta的大型概念模型。
• [nullc] 指出即使在人类语言上训练，token可能有仅对AI可读的"潜台词"，并且AI无法向我们解释。训练推理可能会放大潜台词，因为随机噪声若与正确结果偶然相关会被放大。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于CoT方法的实际作用机制和其有效性背后的原因。部分评论者认为CoT方法帮助模型获得了更多的计算时间，而非实际的文字意义。
• 对"Unreasonable Effectiveness"模式的过度使用表示不满，认为其失去了最初的神秘性和哲学深度。
• 讨论还涉及模型训练中的"潜台词"问题，以及如何通过不同的训练方法来减少噪声的影响。

data.title: Positional preferences, order effects, prompt sensitivity undermine AI judgments
data.author: joalstein
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）在敏感领域（如招聘、医疗、法律等）中作为决策工具时存在的不可靠性问题。作者指出，尽管通过各种方式（如A/B决策、排名、分类等）使用LLM做出决策，但每种方法都存在脆弱性，并受到鲜少讨论的测量偏见影响。文章强调了"提示工程"实践中依赖未经严格测试的模板和方法，导致决策结果易受提示方式、问题表述和标签选择的影响。LLM表现出与人类相似的认知偏见，如位置偏好、顺序效应和锚定效应。例如，在成对选择时，LLM更倾向于选择"选项B"；在评分时，评分顺序和上下文会影响结果；此外，LLM对负性特质的评分往往偏中或偏低。文章呼吁对LLM决策的不可预测性和潜在偏见保持警惕。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的敏感性、判断力及其在实际应用中的局限和潜力

不同观点：
• **nowittyusername** 认为LLM对系统提示的顺序、语言使用、长度、示例的详细程度等非常敏感，这些变量会影响输出质量。他们指出，LLM基于标记进行“推理和思考”，并没有内部世界表示，因此输出会因语言不同而变化。他们正在开发一种自动校准系统，以找到与特定LLM沟通的最佳方式。

• **SrslyJosh** 指出，LLM对提示的敏感性说明其缺乏实际的“判断力”。如果LLM具备强大的逻辑基础，输入的细微差异不应导致输出质量的不稳定。

• **shahbaby** 赞同SrslyJosh的观点，认为LLM不擅长需要评估的任务，否则可以完全取代人类实现自我改进的AGI（通用人工智能）。

• **nimitkalra** 提到已知的其他分布偏差，如自我偏好偏差和结构化输出偏差，并提供了一些校准和稳定这些偏差的资源和方法。

• **TrackerFF** 对“评审小组”的弱点提出质疑，认为多模态分布不太可能在大小组中发生，除非只有两个结果（如yes/no）的情况。

• **PrimordialEdg71** 认为LLM可以作为临时的评分者，但其判断会随提示的措辞和选项顺序而大幅波动，建议通过随机输入、集成输出和保持人类参与来改善准确性。

• **armchairhacker** 认为LLM在发现知识方面有优势，可以辅助真实的法官、科学家、医生等专业人士，但必须对LLM的输出进行验证。

• **tempodox** 对“提示工程”持怀疑态度，称之为“提示猜测”，认为其像是现代的炼金术。

• **sidcool** 认为从“不可能”到“不可靠”的进步对技术人员是好方向，但对社会学家或人类学家则不一定。

• **photochemsyn** 提到未将DeepSeek与OpenAI和Gemini进行基准测试，并提供了一些关于如何有效使用提示工程的建议。

• **giancarlostoro** 不希望LLM对关键问题有最终决定权，认为LLM应识别需要后续审查的内容，由合格人员确认。

• **lyu07282** 观察到工具调用的参数顺序会影响性能，强调在构建上下文时需要非常谨慎。

• **sanqui** 提到爱沙尼亚决定用AI解决儿童抚养纠纷，暗示对LLM在法律应用中的信任。

• **devmor** 认为LLM是统计数据库，不是逻辑引擎，不能进行逻辑、推理或判断，其表现只是对人类交流的统计相似性的复制，不具备真正的智能。

补充讨论：
- LLM的提示敏感性和分布偏差是讨论的焦点，提示工程的有效性和自动化校准系统被提出作为解决方案。
- LLM在发现知识和辅助专业人士方面的潜力被认可，但需要人类验证以确保准确性。
- LLM在法律和社会应用中的伦理和实际效果受到质疑。

44074668.article_content:
LLM Judges Are Unreliable
May 22
Written By
James Padolsey
How Positional Preferences, Order Effects, and Prompt Sensitivity Undermine Reliability in AI Judgments
By
James Padolsey
Beyond their everyday chat capabilities, Large Language Models are increasingly being used to make decisions in sensitive domains like hiring, health, law, and civic engagement. The exact mechanics of how we use these models in such scenarios is vital. There are many ways to have LLMs make decisions, including A/B decision-making, ranking, classification, "panels" of judges, etc. but every single method is individually fragile and subject to measurement biases that are rarely discussed.
Engineers composing prompts often rely on anecdotes and untested folklore. We call it 'prompt-engineering': the practice of composing prompts to coax precisely the outputs we desire. However, it might be described better as 'playing' than 'engineering'. There are popular templates and tropes, but few are well proven. You'll often see high level instructions like "you are an [adjective] [role]", e.g. "you are an impartial judge". Throw in a superlative here and there, maybe some ALL-CAPS and a few examples, run it a couple of times, observe it working, and then stamp 'shipped'. In doing all of this, there is an implicit buy-in into a premise that LLMs are sufficiently predictable when asked 'just right' for a limited set of outputs, a premise that ongoing research continues to challenge [3].
But even if you give an LLM just two options of equal merit and ask it for the best, it will tilt one way or the other. Or give it an essay to judge according to a few criteria, and you will see its score subtly shift by how we pose the question. Filtering and classification tasks too, like detecting toxicity or cyber-bullying, are highly fragile. Ranking CVs from job applicants is a famously hard problem fraught with social biases. We know this, but rarely do we consider the very ‘posing of the problem’ to an AI to be a massive lever of bias as well.
Such unpredictability is rare in computation, but it's very similar to human cognition. LLMs consistently exhibit vulnerabilities and cognitive biases like our own [4, 5, 6, 7], including serial position, framing, and anchoring. This is observable; we've conducted many tests on 'frontier' models from Google, Mistral, Microsoft, X, Anthropic and OpenAI and have seen consistent expression of biases in judgement contexts, from small-parameter to larger parameter reasoning models alike:
Pairwise Choice - Positional & Labeling Biases
: When tasked with choosing between 'Response A' and 'Response B' over numerous trials, LLMs tended to select 'Response B' approximately 60% - 69% of the time (our suite's aggregated data across 8 models showed 'Response B' preferred ~61% of the time). This significant deviation from random choice [1] highlights a volatile positional preference. Minor changes in prompt phrasing or label nature (e.g., 'Response A/B' vs. '(A)/(B)') can swing this preference by 5-10 percentage points or more. While abstract, non-sequential labels (e.g., 'ID_123' or '❖') diminished this bias by 4-7 percentage points in our tests, a notable preference often remained, underscoring the critical impact of labeling strategy [1]. This mirrors human cognitive biases where order and labelling effects are well-documented [6, 7].
Rubric-Based Scoring - Order & Context Effects
: When scoring items against multiple criteria (e.g., Clarity, Logic, Conciseness), the order of presentation significantly alters results. Our aggregated data showed a criterion like 'Clarity' decreasing in its average score by approximately 3.5% when evaluated last versus earlier, indicating a 'recency bias' [4]. Furthermore, the evaluation context (holistic vs. isolated criteria) dramatically impacts scores, though variably. For instance, one model scored an argument's 'Clarity' at 5.0/5 in isolation but 4.0/5 when scored holistically with other criteria for the same item—a full-point drop. Generally, holistic evaluation tends to dilute scores for negative traits (e.g., "sexism" from other rubrics) compared to isolated evaluation.
Scale Interpretation & Negative Trait Biases
: LLMs often bring a prior that "higher is better" from training data (e.g., 5/5 stars = good). This clashes with tasks requiring scoring of negative traits (toxicity, sexism) on ascending scales where "higher" means "worse." This can lead to models compressing scores towards the middle or low end, understating severity (e.g., labeling "Very High" toxicity as "Moderate") [8]. The scale format itself is a major factor: our broader research on "presence of sexism" showed a 1-5 numerical scale yielding an average score of 1.68, while an A-E categorical scale for the exact same item and criterion produced a score of 3.17 (A=high sexism) [5]. Even limited tests in our data dump confirmed categorical scales tended to elicit slightly less lenient scores for toxicity and sexism.

data.title: The metre originated in the French Revolution
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了米这一长度单位的历史演变，其现代定义于1983年确立，但其起源可追溯至18世纪末的法国大革命时期。当时，为了统一测量标准，数学家和科学家将米定义为通过巴黎从北极到赤道距离的千万分之一。1799年，这一长度被制成一个铂金棒，称为“档案米”。随着科学进步，米的定义多次改变。1960年，米被重新定义为氪-86气体发出的特定光波波长的倍数。1983年，米被再次定义为光在真空中于1/299,792,458秒内行进的距离，这一定义沿用至今。文章还提到《米制公约》于1875年签署，旨在全球范围内统一测量系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于公制系统的历史、准确性、实用性及其争议

不同观点：
• [az09mugen] 提到法国大革命期间曾尝试实行10小时制，每小时100分钟，每分钟100秒，并提供了相关历史链接。
• [skrebbel] 和 [nartho] 对天文科学家们在当时技术条件下取得的精确度表示赞赏，认为仅差0.2毫米是极为了不起的成就。
• [bambax] 分享了一个关于祖父不喜欢公制系统的故事，认为公制系统虽然实用，但缺乏美感，显得僵硬和不讨喜。
• [n1b0m] 提问当初用来测量一米长度的单位是什么，暗示了对历史测量标准的好奇。
• [rippeltippel] 对光速定义米的做法表示质疑，认为这是一种循环定义，感觉不对劲。
• [nancyminusone] 对公制系统的基数10系统表示不满，尤其是千克作为基本单位而非克，认为这在使用导出单位时造成不便。
• [willsoon] 讨论了法国大革命前后的测量混乱，并指出公制系统的建立对法国及全球的影响，同时提到十进制系统的优势。
• [metalman] 认为公制系统的缺乏在一定程度上促成了法国大革命前的商业和贸易问题。
• [BitwiseFool] 作为美国人，分享了使用公制系统在实际生活中（如室内装饰）的便利性，并对IKEA在美国网站上不广泛使用公制表示不满。
• [dudeinjapan] 用讽刺的语气提到即使断头台是法国大革命的产物，也不意味着所有人都应该使用它，暗示了对历史产物不应盲目接受。
• [toolslive] 提出基数12可能比基数10更好，暗示了对公制系统基数选择的质疑。
• [Xmd5a] 提出米的长度并非法国大革命期间发明，而是源自古测量系统和黄金比例，认为公制系统只是对古代测量关系的正式化和十进制化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是公制系统的历史来源及其合理性，[Xmd5a] 详细分析了公制系统与古代测量系统的关系，并提出了一种基于黄金比例的几何构造方法。
• 另一个讨论点是公制系统的实用性和美感之间的平衡，[bambax] 和 [toolslive] 都对公制系统的实用性表示认可，但对其美感和基数选择提出质疑。
• 关于定义的准确性和科学性，[skrebbel]、[nartho] 和 [rippeltippel] 对天文测量和光速定义米的精确性和逻辑性进行了讨论，显示了对科学定义方法的关注。
• 最后，[BitwiseFool] 提出的实际使用问题揭示了公制系统在全球化背景下的实用性和推广问题。

44073867.article_content:
The metre originated in the French Revolution, but its definition has changed many times since
By
Belinda Smith
for
Lab Notes
ABC Science
Topic:
Physics
Tue 20 May
Tuesday 20 May
Tue 20 May 2025 at 3:01am
The current definition of the metre was adopted in 1983, but its history stretches back more than 200 years.
(
Getty Images: Olena Ruban
)
abc.net.au/news/metre-treaty-anniversary-metric-system-measurement-metrology/105302024
Link copied
Share
Share
article
The next time you pick up a bag of spuds from the supermarket or fill up the car with petrol, you can thank a treaty signed 150 years ago for the metric system that underpins daily life.
On May 20, 1875, delegates from 17 countries assembled on a Parisian spring day and
signed the Metre Convention
, also known as the Treaty of the Metre.
At the time, it wasn't uncommon for countries, states and even cities to have entirely different ways of measuring distance and mass, hampering trade and holding back progress in science.
Loading...
To standardise and unify these definitions, the Treaty of the Metre established the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, which initially defined the metre and kilogram.
Over the years, more countries signed the Treaty of the Metre, including Australia in November 1947.
A handful of other units of measurement were also included to form the International System of Units, the basis of the metric system.
But the metre's inception predates the treaty that bears its name by nearly 100 years.
And its story begins during the French Revolution.
The metre through history
During the late 1700s, revolutionaries shaping the new republic of France shed old traditions bound to royalty and religion.
The Unity Festival in Revolution Square, as depicted by French artist Pierre-Antoine Démachy, was held on August 10, 1793 to promote the values of the French Republic.
(
Getty Images: Philippe Lissac
)
This reinvention included creating a new system of measurement.
This system would be available to everyone, and be tied to fundamental properties of nature, "not from the length of the king's arm, or something that changed over time", Bruce Warrington, CEO and chief metrologist at the National Measurement Institute, says.
So mathematicians and scientists of the time decreed that the length of a metre — from the Greek word "metron", meaning "a measure" — was equal to one 10-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator through the Paris Observatory.
This line through Paris, called the Paris meridian, featured in Dan Brown's novel The Da Vinci Code.
(
Wikimedia Commons: US Government,
CC0
)
It fell to a pair of astronomers to calculate this distance, and after seven years, in 1799, they presented their final measurement to the French Academy of Sciences which made a "Metre of the Archives" in the form of a platinum bar.
(It was later found the astronomers were a bit off in their calculations, and
the metre as we know it is 0.2 millimetres shorter than it should've been
.)
The Metre of the Archives and its copies were eventually replaced by around 30 metre bars made of a stable platinum-iridium alloy. They were distributed around the world in the late 1890s, and remained the "standard" metre for decades.
National metre prototype 27 was sent to the US and received by President Benjamin Harrison on January 2, 1890.
(
Supplied: NIST Research Library & Museum
)
But as science progressed, the definition of the metre changed too.
This change started early last century, when scientists discovered they could measure distances using light.
Light travels in waves. If you know the distance between each wave — called the wavelength, literally the length of the wave — it's possible to use light "as a very fine ruler", Dr Warrington says.
And in 1960, the platinum alloy bars were out and a new definition of the metre was introduced.
Pass an electrical current through a lamp filled with krypton gas and the krypton atoms throw off light, including a reddish orange wavelength.
Krypton-86 gas is odourless, colourless and exists in tiny quantities in the atmosphere.
(
Supplied: National Institute of Standards and Technology Digital Collections, Gaithersburg, MD 20899
)
One metre equalled 1,650,763.73 times the wavelength of this specific reddish orange light.
Meanwhile, electronics fabrication kicked off and the scale of manufacturing shrunk to the incredibly tiny. Think transistors in a smartphone integrated circuit, which are only a few billionths of a metre wide.
"So you need rulers that can check for and control the quality of that manufacturing at that level," Dr Warrington says — something the krypton lamp metre definition could not do.
Since 1960, there'd been a lot of progress made on measuring time accurately with atomic clocks. Their "ticking" is produced by oscillations of radiation emitted when atoms are bathed in laser light.
And they can tick billions of times every second. This new ability to divvy up the second into increasingly
44073867.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了米这一长度单位的历史演变，其现代定义于1983年确立，但其起源可追溯至18世纪末的法国大革命时期。当时，为了统一测量标准，数学家和科学家将米定义为通过巴黎从北极到赤道距离的千万分之一。1799年，这一长度被制成一个铂金棒，称为“档案米”。随着科学进步，米的定义多次改变。1960年，米被重新定义为氪-86气体发出的特定光波波长的倍数。1983年，米被再次定义为光在真空中于1/299,792,458秒内行进的距离，这一定义沿用至今。文章还提到《米制公约》于1875年签署，旨在全球范围内统一测量系统。

data.title: Designing type inference for high quality type errors
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了类型推断导致编译器产生难以理解的错误信息的问题，并指出这是现有语言设计中为了其他目标而做出的选择，而非类型推断本身的问题。文章介绍了一种名为PolySubML的实验性编程语言，该语言结合了全局类型推断、子类型和高级多态性，并注重提供良好的错误信息。文章解释了设计良好错误信息的重要性，强调编译器应明确证明代码为何无效，并帮助用户找到错误的根源。文章还提到，避免猜测或回溯是设计良好错误信息的关键，并通过具体例子（如特定情况下的类型推断和重载）说明现有语言在错误信息设计上的不足。最后，作者指出PolySubML是一个概念验证项目，而非广泛应用的语言。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编译器错误信息的目的及其在处理代码验证和类型推断中的作用

不同观点：
• johnbender 认为，编译器错误信息的作用是向用户解释为什么编译器无法证明代码是正确的，而不是简单地证明代码无效。他指出，代码可能是有效的，但由于编译器的分析可能不完备，它无法证明其正确性。

• tayistay 分享了其在类型检查器中的实践经验，采用了迭代方式处理约束集并应用推导规则，避免猜测和回溯。如果无法处理过多的重载，类型检查器会让用户添加类型注解。这种方法虽然在某些有效程序上可能无法工作，但实际效果良好。

• renox 对类型推断和函数重载的价值提出疑问，表示对全局类型推断不如对局部类型推断那样看重，反映出对不同语言特性优先级的不同看法。

• init1 强调了Ada语言在类型安全方面的卓越表现，认为其在这方面无与伦比，暗示其他语言在类型安全性上可能不及Ada。

• ruuda 提供了其在RCL语言中实现类型检查器时处理类型不匹配报告的方法，并给出了一个链接供参考，展示了具体的实现细节。

• estbank 提出一个激进的观点，认为编译器的主要角色是将格式错误的代码转化为人类可读的诊断信息，编译器的次要角色才是代码生成，突显了错误报告在编译器设计中的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对编译器错误信息的不同理解和实际实现中的技术选择，如迭代处理和类型注解的应用。
• 不同参与者对类型推断和函数重载的价值有不同的看法，反映出在语言设计和实现中存在优先级和取舍的讨论。
• 争议的焦点之一是编译器错误信息的主要目的，以及在类型检查过程中如何处理无法证明代码正确的情况。

44032995.article_content:
Type inference has a reputation for causing unhelpful error messages from the compiler when there is a type error. For example, here’s a typical comment:
I started a project at work with flowjs, got inscrutable type errors in a different file than wherever the root cause was and bailed for typescript.
However, things don’t have to be this way. Type inference’s bad reputation is due to design decisions in existing languages that sacrifice good error messages in exchange for other goals. There is nothing inherent to type inference that prevents you from offering good error messages.
I recently released
PolySubML
, a programming language combining global type inference with subtyping and advanced polymorphism, and supporting good type error messages was a constant consideration during development. In this post, I will explain how I designed PolySubML’s error messages and why I think existing languages tend to fall short in this respect.
But first, a few disclaimers:
First off, this post is solely concerned with error messages for
type errors
. Dealing with
syntax errors
, particularly parser errors, is a completely different topic that is outside the scope of this post.
Second, the focus here is helping the user to
understand why their code won’t compile
and identify the cause of the error. In some cases, compilers will also attempt to guess what the user meant and suggest a fix, but this is inherently heuristic-based and subjective, and outside the scope of this post.
Lastly, PolySubML is an experimental hobby programming language that has never been used at large scale. It is a
proof of concept
and
demonstration
of my ideas, but it is a very different sort of beast than widespread battle-tested languages. Since PolySubML is a one-person hobby project, the focus is on the
underlying algorithms
and design aspects, rather than aspects like polish which are a function of time and people (the Rust compiler in particular has had almost infinite polish applied over the years, thanks to its incredibly large and dedicated community.)
With that out of the way, let’s get on to the pitfalls that often make compiler error messages suck:
Rule 1: Never guess or backtrack
Generally speaking, users think their code is correct when submitting it to the compiler. Sometimes, people will speculatively compile to try to identify bugs or places that need to be updated during a refactor, but even then, the user merely thinks that there might be bugs
somewhere
in the abstract. They won’t be convinced of the presence of bugs unless the compiler provides specific evidence explaining where and why there is a bug. (Or rather, a violation of the language’s typing rules which
often
but not necessarily indicates a bug.)
The job of a compiler error message is to prove to the user that their code is invalid
according to the language’s rules, ideally in a way that helps the user identify where they went wrong and how the problem can be corrected.
Abstractly, the process of type checking can be modeled as deriving
a set of facts
about the code, with specific rules for deriving new facts based on previous facts, with the rules determined by the language. For example, you might have reasoning along the lines of “
4
has type int” and “if
4
has type int, then after
let x = 4
,
x
also has type int” and “in
x.foo
,
x
is required to be a record”, and “if an expression of type int is used as a record, the program is invalid”.
The general form of the rules is “if A and B and C, then D”, where the typechecker continually derives facts from the right hand side of rules once the left hand side is satisfied. Eventually it either derives a contradiction and reports a type error, or it doesn’t and the code compiles successfully. This leads to proofs that are relatively short and easy to understand - once a contradiction is reached, you can easily work backwards and show the user a sequence explaining exactly why their code is invalid, step by step. (Realistically, you probably don’t want to show the user
every
step for reasons of verbosity, but the point is that you
could
if necessary. More on this in section 3.)
However, this all goes wrong if your language includes rules of the form “if A and B and C, then D
or E
”. Suddenly, instead of proceeding monotonically from start to finish, the compiler has to
guess
how to proceed. This means that the compiler has to try
every possibility
in order to discover a type error. For example, if you know A, B, and C, that lets you conclude “D or E”, but “D or E” doesn’t help at all by itself. If say, D turns out to lead to a contradiction, you can’t immediately report an error like before - instead you have to backtrack and see if E leads to a contradiction
too
.
Ad-hoc overloading
The above description is very abstract, so let’s look at a more concrete example - specifically
ad hoc overloading
. In some languages, you might have multiple different functions with the same name and different type signatures, and the compi

data.title: Making Postgres Distributed with FoundationDB
data.author: emptysea
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了将Postgres转变为分布式数据库的探索过程，并提到了一些现有方案的局限性。Citus需要手动配置，CockroachDB并非真正的Postgres且不开源，Neon虽然是Postgres扩展但并非完全多主分布式。作者因此开发了实验性开源扩展pgfdb，使Postgres成为无状态层，依托FoundationDB实现扩展性、弹性和事务保证。pgfdb通过自定义访问方法替换存储和事务引擎，充分利用FoundationDB的分布式特性。尽管pgfdb仍在早期实验阶段，性能有待验证，但展示了Postgres的高度可扩展性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于新项目的技术实现和潜力的讨论]

不同观点：
• [atombender] 认为该项目并没有取代低级别的页堆存储，而是通过插件机制提供了表和索引的新实现，分别称为表访问方法和索引访问方法。他将此机制比作SQLite的虚拟表机制，但认为C API更友好。他还提到，尽管过去有人批评Postgres的可插拔引擎接口不够灵活，但这个项目显示出其灵活性和丰富性，可能受益于OrioleDB和Citus等开发的替代表引擎的近期工作。

• [fabianlindfors] 作为项目作者，对评论表示感谢，并表示愿意回答任何问题。这表明他对项目的高度参与和开放态度。

• [bithavoc] 将该项目与YugabyteDB进行类比，认为它在FoundationDB之上实现类似于YugabyteDB的功能。这暗示了对该项目在分布式数据库领域潜力的关注。

补充讨论：
• [atombender] 提到对Postgres扩展API的印象有所改观，特别是对其灵活性和丰富性的新认识，可能与近期其他开发者的工作有关。

• [bithavoc] 的评论引发了对该项目与YugabyteDB相似性的讨论，提示了该项目在技术架构上可能具有的创新性和应用场景。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点可能在于该项目是否真的如[atombender]所说，具有高度的灵活性和丰富性，还是需要更多的实际应用验证。此外，与YugabyteDB的类比也可能引发关于其定位和竞争力的讨论。

44072738.article_content:
Fabian Lindfors
Making Postgres distributed with FoundationDB
← All posts
· 22 May 2025
Turning the revered Postgres into a distributed database is a tall order but not a new idea. It has been done in many different ways with different characteristics.
Citus
requires a fair bit of manual configuration and client setup, but is open-source and distributed as an extension.
CockroachDB
is simpler to integrate but is not actually Postgres and not open-source.
Neon
is perhaps the most interesting being a true Postgres extension and having some compelling features, but isn’t fully distributed in the multi-master sense.
None of these quite scratched my itch for what a distributed Postgres could look like, so I couldn’t help but try to scratch it myself. The result of that is
pgfdb
, an experimental, open-source extension for Postgres that turns it into a stateless layer on top of
FoundationDB
. This means full compatibility with Postgres (it
is
Postgres) with the scalability, resiliency and transactional guarantees of FoundationDB.
Being able to build such a project is a testament to just how extensible Postgres is. pgfdb uses a number of Postgres extension points, like custom table and index access methods, to fully replace the standard storage and transaction engines. This means table and index data is stored and read in a way that suits FoundationDB, and full use is made of FoundationDB’s distributed transaction processing.
pgfdb is still very experimental and it remains to be seen if acceptable performance can even be achieved for a typical Postgres workload, but I wanted to put it out there early. If you are interested in chatting about it, please
reach out
!

data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种在Isabelle/HOL中对有界复杂度的丢番图方程进行形式化验证的通用构造。作者通过形式化验证，确认了在特定变量数和次数限制下，丢番图方程的不可判定性。这一工作扩展了Isabelle中多变量多项式的理论，并为处理复杂多项式定义提供了元编程基础设施。研究展示了数学家与计算机协作的潜力，通过定理证明器大大推进了研究进程。文章共16页，包含一个图示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MRDP定理及其相关未解问题和实际应用

不同观点：
• [kevinventullo] 强调MRDP定理的一个惊人结果，即存在一个多变量多项式，其第一个变量的整数解对应的值恰好是素数集合。他提供了一个链接，指向有关素数公式的维基百科页面，以支持其观点。

• [MJGrzymek] 认为未解的问题中，哪些（变量数量，次数）组合对于MRDP是不可判定的，这一问题被低估了。他提出，这些组合的答案是有限的，并且可以列举出最小的不可判定组合。如果限制变量数量、次数以及系数的最大绝对值，那么这个问题是可判定的，因为有限性决定了可判定性。

• [btilly] 提供了一个更易理解的总结，指出任何丢番图方程可以被简化为最多11个变量且次数最高约为10^63的方程。对于这一类丢番图方程，没有算法可以决定其在有理数范围内的可解性。

补充讨论：
• [nine_k] 提出了一个实际应用的问题，询问MRDP定理的这一结果是否对密码学有任何实际影响。

• [badmonster] 对MRDP定理的形式化工作表示赞赏，认为这是深度数论和形式方法之间的一项令人印象深刻的桥梁工作。

- 目前讨论中没有明显的对立观点，但存在对MRDP定理未解问题的不同关注点，一些人关注理论上的不可判定性（MJGrzymek），另一些人则关注实际应用和理解（btilly, nine_k）。

讨论围绕MRDP定理的惊人结果、未解问题的不可判定性、以及其在密码学中的潜在应用展开。参与者对定理的理论意义和实际应用价值有不同侧重的讨论。

Title:
A Formal Proof of Complexity Bounds on Diophantine Equations
Authors:
Jonas Bayer
,
Marco David
View a PDF of the paper titled A Formal Proof of Complexity Bounds on Diophantine Equations, by Jonas Bayer and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a universal construction of Diophantine equations with bounded complexity in Isabelle/HOL. This is a formalization of our own work in number theory.
Hilbert's Tenth Problem was answered negatively by Yuri Matiyasevich, who showed that there is no general algorithm to decide whether an arbitrary Diophantine equation has a solution. However, the problem remains open when generalized to the field of rational numbers, or contrarily, when restricted to Diophantine equations with bounded complexity, characterized by the number of variables $\nu$ and the degree $\delta$. If every Diophantine set can be represented within the bounds $(\nu, \delta)$, we say that this pair is universal, and it follows that the corresponding class of equations is undecidable. In a separate mathematics article, we have determined the first non-trivial universal pair for the case of integer unknowns.
In this paper, we contribute a formal verification of the main construction required to establish said universal pair. In doing so, we markedly extend the Isabelle AFP entry on multivariate polynomials, formalize parts of a number theory textbook, and develop classical theory on Diophantine equations in Isabelle. Additionally, our work includes metaprogramming infrastructure designed to efficiently handle complex definitions of multivariate polynomials. Our mathematical draft has been formalized while the mathematical research was ongoing, and benefitted largely from the help of the theorem prover. We reflect how the close collaboration between mathematician and computer is an uncommon but promising modus operandi.

data.author: randomor

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一款新推出的苹果应用的评价和反馈，涵盖了用户体验、功能设计、定价策略、技术集成以及跨平台支持等方面。

不同观点：
• [allenu] 认为应用的界面截图很吸引人，但建议简化着陆页的文字说明，让用户更容易理解应用的核心功能。他还提到了一些用户体验上的小问题，比如搜索框未自动对焦，以及快捷键操作不符合预期。
• [kstrauser] 对应用的功能和隐私保护表示赞赏，但对定价持保留态度，认为相对于同类产品价格偏高。他还指出快捷键说明容易引起误解。
• [stevelacy] 建议隐藏主窗口以改善用户体验，并提供了技术上的建议（NSApplication.setActivationPolicy(.accessory)）。
• [raydenvm] 对选择 "Cmd + C" 两次作为快捷键表示好奇，并询问是否有其他不冲突的快捷键选项。
• [mnming] 提出了对专门书签工具的需求质疑，认为Notion和Obsidian等工具已经能满足需求。
• [iJohnDoe] 作为一个长期Mac用户，寻求推荐Mac专用的AI/LLM应用，以作为购买新MacBook的动力。
• [G1N] 对定价信息在网站上不明显表示不满，认为应该更容易找到。
• [awaseem] 表示正在开发类似工具，对应用是否免费表示关注。
• [Jotalea] 认为此类功能应内置于macOS，并对应用仅支持苹果系统表示失望。
• [loremm] 表达了对Linux支持的渴望，即便实现不够完美也愿意尝试。
• [asadm] 希望应用能提供一次性购买选项，而不是订阅制，反映了对订阅制的疲劳。
• [jonator] 询问应用是否有MCP服务器支持。
• [mdonahoe] 只是简单提及了应用的名字，未做详细评论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是应用的定价策略，部分用户认为相对于类似产品价格偏高。
• 另一个值得注意的点是用户对跨平台支持的期望，尤其是Linux用户。
• 快捷键设计和用户体验细节（如搜索框自动对焦）也是用户关注的重点，提出了具体的改进建议。
• 隐私保护和数据收集问题也得到了积极评价，显示出用户对此方面的高度关注。

data.title: Show HN: Genetic Boids Web Simulation
data.author: vimgrinder
data.article_summary: 《GeneticBoids》是一篇关于模拟群体行为（Boids）的参数设置说明，由@attentionmech编写。文章描述了一个包含500个Boid个体的群体，具有不同的运动参数、群体行为规则（如对齐、分离、凝聚）、感知范围、遗传信号机制及视觉表现设置。Boid的寿命设定为2000，遗传信号的概率为0.002，范围为50，信号力为0.1，基因组长度为6。此外，还提供了多种预设模式（如 calm、chaotic、swarm 等）和性能调节选项（如网格大小、帧率目标）。文章最后列出了一些动态统计数据如FPS、活跃信号、平均速度、集群数量等，并提供了多种控制按钮如重置、随机化等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Boids模拟及其不同实现、优化和应用

不同观点：
• [talkingtab] 认为Craig Reynolds的原始Boids实现非常逼真，尤其是其基于三种“引导”机制的运动效果，而其他版本则更像简单的模拟，缺乏真实感。他提出了对不同版本差异的原因进行探讨的兴趣，并初步分析了代码中的适应度函数。

• [animal531] 分享了使用RVO2 ORCA方法的体验，并通过视频展示了其优化和性能改进。他指出该方法在高密度环境下有效，但计算成本较高，需要对邻近对象进行大量计算。

• [brodo] 提到使用Go和WebGPU实现的Boids模拟，能够在M1 Mac Pro上轻松处理16k Boids，且未进行任何优化。

• [Xevion] 对展示的Boids模拟表示赞赏，并提出了一些改进建议，包括颜色优化、缩放和交互功能，以及通过GPU优化提升性能的建议。

• [anigbrowl] 表示在使用Vivaldi浏览器时，模拟在大约30秒后崩溃，指出了潜在的兼容性或性能问题。

补充讨论：
• [vladde] 提到了一个类似的通过简单规则创建生命行为的例子，并提供了一个视频链接，展示了一些有趣的案例。

• [kldavis4] 询问了遗传算法在Boids模拟中的应用。

• [brulard] 对Boids模拟中“信号”的概念表示好奇。

• [rvnx] 表示首次了解Boids，并对其表示赞赏。

• [throw_m239339] 回忆起在Blender中使用Boids模拟来模仿鸟群的经历，并对设置的复杂性表示困惑。

争议焦点：
• 不同Boids实现的真实感差异及其原因。
• Boids模拟在不同硬件和软件环境下的性能表现和稳定性问题。

data.title: Types of optical systems in a lens designer's toolbox (2020)
data.author: picture
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一份关于镜头设计形式的终极指南，涵盖了各种光学系统及其应用。文章探讨了基本和重要的镜头设计形式，包括单透镜、双透镜、三合透镜、天塞透镜、双高斯透镜等，并解释了它们的发展和用途。文章还讨论了现代镜头设计，如非球面镜头、自由曲面镜头和用于手机摄像头的镜头，以及特殊用途的镜头系统，如鱼眼镜头、变焦镜头和反射光学镜头。此外，文章提供了对镜头设计背后原理的深入理解，帮助读者在面对规格表时更好地选择和设计镜头。文章最后还提到使用计算软件进行镜头设计的现代方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：光学镜头设计工具和资源

不同观点：
• [alexbock] 提供了一个免费且开源的网页用户界面（UI），用于镜头设计，支持模拟双高斯镜头等设计。该工具允许用户操作镜头参数并观察效果，适合希望动手实验的用户。
• [Xmd5a] 提到了一个针对非专业人士的指南，指出该指南不适合那些愿意成为镜头设计“狂热者”的人。此外，Xmd5a 分享了自己在近红外光谱仪项目中通过试错法确定柱面镜最佳位置的经验，而没有进行严格的计算。
• [contingencies] 推荐了一本关于大画幅相机技术的书《View Camera Technique: 7th Edition》，认为其插图精美且内容有趣。此外，分享了在东莞遇到的从事iPhone镜头组装工作的韩国专家，指出高端镜头组装涉及多达13个镜片元素，每个组件都需要根据其具体光学特性进行数字化校正。
• [joshvm] 表达了对使用Mathematica中的Optica插件进行光学设计的兴趣，但指出该插件价格高昂，且很少遇到使用该工具的人，尽管学术界通常可以免费获得Mathematica。
• [elikoga] 提到了一个与“Torch Lens Maker”相关的项目，这是一个基于PyTorch的可微分几何光学工具，适合对光学模拟感兴趣的开发者。
• [NKosmatos] 试图寻找一个曾经使用过的镜头和光源模拟器，但未能找到相关链接，寻求社区帮助以找到该资源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的工具和资源包括免费开源的网页工具、书籍推荐、商业软件插件以及基于Python的开发工具，展示了不同用户在镜头设计中的多样化需求和方法。
• 争议的焦点可能在于工具的获取和使用成本，例如Mathematica插件的高价让一些用户望而却步，而免费开源工具则更受欢迎。
• 用户分享了实际项目中的经验（如Xmd5a的试错法）以及行业专家的实践（如contingencies提到的iPhone镜头组装），为讨论增加了实际应用的视角。

data.title: Japan and the Birth of Modern Shipbuilding
data.author: m463
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了日本如何在二战后吸收美国战时快速造船技术，并发展出现代造船业。二战期间，美国通过焊接和预制件组装的方法迅速建造大量船只，但战后这一体系被解散。美国实业家如亨利·凯瑟和丹尼尔·路德维希将这一技术带到日本，特别是在吴市造船厂进行大型油轮的建造。吴市曾是二战时建造世界上最大战舰“大和号”的地方，拥有先进的设施。路德维希在吴建造了一系列破纪录的大型油轮，包括1958年世界上首个超过10万吨的“宇宙阿波罗号”。通过结合预制件、焊接和工业流程改进策略，日本发展出更快、更便宜的现代造船方法，最终主导了全球造船市场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本与美国在战后造船业的比较及其对经济和技能发展的影响

不同观点：
• DrNosferatu认为，欧盟当前的自由经济理论强调国家不应干预经济，但这一点应该重新审视，特别是在了解了日本战后造船业的成功经验后。
• alephnerd指出，日本战后造船业的薪资相对于全国平均水平较高，约为160%，这吸引了高技能工人进入该行业。相比之下，美国和加拿大在同时期没有类似的薪资差距。日本将造船业视为工程/STEM学科，而美国则视为蓝领半技能职业。alephnerd还提到，类似的趋势在韩国以及其他行业（如芯片设计、VFX、电池制造等）中也能观察到。他还比较了美国与以色列、印度及中东欧在教育系统上的不同，后者更注重系统和架构基础。
• dumdedum123对alephnerd的观点持怀疑态度，认为美国在二战期间发明了现代造船技术，而日本只是复制并发展了这些技术。

补充讨论：
• rufus_foreman提供了数据支持，指出在战争高峰期，美国生产了全球近90%的船舶，但到1950年代，这一比例下降到略高于2%。这一数据为讨论提供了历史背景，说明美国在造船业的显著变化。
• alephnerd的观点引用了多个来源支持其论点，包括关于日本战后薪资的数据和关于造船业工程学科定位的历史文章。
• 争议的焦点在于日本造船业的成功是否主要归因于复制美国技术并加以发展，还是由于其他因素（如薪资激励、技能水平等）推动了其成功。

How Japan invented modern shipbuilding, and conquered the shipbuilding industry in the process.

Universe Apollo, first 100,000 DWT supertanker, built by National Bulk Carriers at Kure, Japan.
During WWII, the US constructed an unprecedented shipbuilding machine. By assembling ships from welded, prefabricated blocks, the US built a huge number of cargo ships incredibly quickly, overwhelming Germany’s u-boats and helping to win the war. But when the war was over, this shipbuilding machine was dismantled. Industrialists like Henry Kaiser and Stephen Bechtel, who operated some of the US’s most efficient wartime shipyards, left the shipbuilding business. Prior to the war, the US had been an uncompetitive commercial shipbuilder producing a small fraction of commercial oceangoing ships, and that’s what it became again. At the height of the war the US was producing nearly 90% of the world’s ships. By the 1950s, it produced just over 2%.
But the lessons from the US’s shipbuilding machine weren’t forgotten. After the war, practitioners brought them to Japan, where they would continue to evolve, eventually allowing Japan to build ships faster and cheaper than almost anyone else in the world.
Origins of Japan’s post-war shipbuilding industry
One of the shipyards that built cargo ships during the war was
Welding Shipyards
, owned by Daniel Ludwig. In 1936 Ludwig had founded shipping company National Bulk Carriers (NBC), which bought surplus WWI cargo ships and converted them into oil tankers. From there, Ludwig expanded into shipbuilding, and built his one-berth shipyard at Norfolk in 1940.
1
During the war, Welding Shipyards produced T3 tankers using prefabricated welded construction, which were then operated by National Bulk Carriers. After the war, Ludwig continued to build tankers: between 1948 and 1950 he built 5
Bulkpetrol-class tankers
, then the largest tankers in the world.
Ludwig wanted to build even larger ships, in part to capitalize on the burgeoning iron ore trade with Venezuela, but was limited by the size of the berth at Welding Shipyards. Unfazed, Ludwig dispatched his lieutenant Elmer Hann to find a shipyard with the capacity to build larger vessels. The search brought Hann to a former naval shipyard in Kure, Japan, near Hiroshima. The Kure facilities were enormous: they had been used to build the
Yamato
, the largest battleship in the world, and had a 100-ton gantry crane and a drydock capable of building ships of 150,000 tons deadweight. (By comparison, a Liberty ship is about 10,800 deadweight tons.) In 1951, Ludwig signed a 10-year lease for the Kure shipyard.
At Kure, National Bulk Carriers built a series of record-breakingly large ships: the 38,000 deadweight ton Petro Kure in 1952, the 45,000 deadweight ton Phoenix in 1954, and the 55,000 deadweight ton Sinclair Petro-Lore in 1955. The
Universe Apollo
, launched at Kure in 1958, was the first tanker in the world to exceed 100,000 deadweight tons. Altogether Ludwig built 42 ships at Kure, many of them the largest in the world when completed. When his lease at Kure expired, the shipyards were acquired by Japanese shipbuilder IHI, which continued to build enormous tankers for Ludwig.
Kure and modern shipbuilding methods
Modern shipbuilding methods were born at Kure in the 1950s, by combining three different strategies for industrial process improvement.
The first strategy was the prefabricated, welded shipbuilding methods that the US had used so successfully during WWII. To briefly recap, prior to WWII ships were largely built in-place by riveting together the hull one piece at a time. This was time-consuming (a Liberty-sized ship could take months to produce) and labor-intensive, in part because riveting took a long time, and in part because so much of the work was done in the confines of the partially-built ship. Replacing riveting with welding allowed for faster assembly, and also saved steel (since welded plates didn’t need to overlap like riveted plates did). And by constructing the ship out of large, prefabricated blocks, work could be moved out of the confines of the ship and into specialized assembly areas where it could be more easily performed and more workers could work on the ship at once, increasing speed and improving efficiency.
Prefabricated block being lifted into place at Oregonship during WWII.
Both Elmer Hann and Danield Ludwig were well-versed in welded, prefabricated shipbuilding. Ludwig had used it at Welding Shipyards to build T3 and Bulkpetrol-class tankers, and Elmer Hann had been the superintendent for Henry Kaiser’s
Swan Island shipyard
, which used welded, prefabricated construction to produce 147 T2 tankers ov
44075236.article_summary: 本文介绍了日本如何在二战后吸收美国战时快速造船技术，并发展出现代造船业。二战期间，美国通过焊接和预制件组装的方法迅速建造大量船只，但战后这一体系被解散。美国实业家如亨利·凯瑟和丹尼尔·路德维希将这一技术带到日本，特别是在吴市造船厂进行大型油轮的建造。吴市曾是二战时建造世界上最大战舰“大和号”的地方，拥有先进的设施。路德维希在吴建造了一系列破纪录的大型油轮，包括1958年世界上首个超过10万吨的“宇宙阿波罗号”。通过结合预制件、焊接和工业流程改进策略，日本发展出更快、更便宜的现代造船方法，最终主导了全球造船市场。

data.title: Show HN: hcker.news – an ergonomic, timeline-based Hacker News front page
data.author: postalcoder
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Hacker News的一个替代时间线界面（hcker.news），用户可以自定义新闻的展示方式和过滤条件。用户可以选择不同的视图模式（如经典、Hckr、多列），调整主题（浅色、深色等），设置字体大小和密度。此外，还提供高级过滤选项，可以根据标题包含或排除特定关键词，并设置最小投票数来筛选故事。该界面旨在提升用户体验，尤其适合关注独立网络内容的读者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News及其替代前端的用户体验和功能改进

不同观点：
• **支持Hacker News稳定性和开放数据的优点**：
  - jasonthorsness认为Hacker News的核心优势在于其稳定性，链接自2007年以来几乎没有失效，同时对外开放数据，支持第三方创建替代界面，这种用户友好的做法与互联网其他部分的封闭趋势形成对比。

• **介绍和展示自建替代前端的功能**：
  - adrianwaj介绍了自己创建的Hackerbrain网站，强调其快速查看顶部评论和切换评论视图的功能，并对这些功能感到满意。
  - coolwulf分享了自己用Rust构建的开源Hacker News客户端，展示了该客户端的独特性。
  - wvl建议参考hckrnews.com，并提供了一个暗色模式的链接。
  
• **对无JavaScript体验的批评和建议**：
  - koito17指出Hackerbrain网站在禁用JavaScript后完全无法使用，而Hacker News官方前端在这方面处理得更好。建议进行服务器端数据获取以避免页面闪烁，并让用户在JavaScript加载前至少能看到标题。

• **对UI/UX设计的赞赏**：
  - ls-a赞赏Hacker News的UI/UX设计多年无人能及，并询问是否由专业设计师设计。
  
• **功能缺失和建议**：
  - nico表示希望有一个隐藏功能，以便清理已读或不感兴趣的内容。
  - feep询问是否计划加入RSS支持，并感谢hnrss.github.io的创建者，同时表达了对更多过滤功能的期望。
  
• **对随机浏览功能的推荐**：
  - atomic128推荐使用随机浏览功能，认为这是阅读Hacker News的最佳方式，可以避免成瘾性和个人偏见，提供了具体网站https://rnsaffn.com/zg2/作为示例。

• **对自定义配置的需求**：
  - adrianwaj希望看到类似/bestcomments的功能，并询问是否已有类似功能存在。
  - conroydave建议将设置作为URL参数，以便用户可以书签他们的首选配置。

补充讨论：
• **对减少在线时间的需求**：
  - _august表示作为一个试图减少在线时间但仍想保持更新的人，非常喜欢这些替代前端提供的功能。

争议焦点：
• **JavaScript依赖性**：
  - koito17认为Hackerbrain网站在无JavaScript环境下的表现不佳，而官方前端处理得更好，这是功能改进的一个争议点。

• **功能需求差异**：
  - 用户对隐藏功能、RSS支持、自定义配置等功能的需求不同，反映出不同用户在使用Hacker News时的偏好和优先级不同。

data.title: Emacs dired-mode as a file manager
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Guix系统中使用Emacs的Dired模式作为文件管理器，解决文件类型与默认程序关联的问题。作者平时依赖Emacs处理文件，不常使用传统的文件管理器。当从网上下载文件并点击“显示文件夹”时，由于缺少文件管理器，没有任何反应。为解决此问题，作者通过Guix的`home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type`服务配置，将目录的MIME类型`inode/directory`与Emacs的Dired模式关联起来。具体操作包括编写Guile Scheme配置文件，定义一个`.desktop`文件并关联到指定MIME类型，最终实现用Emacs管理文件。通过`guix home reconfigure`命令应用配置，成功解决问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs中的Dired模式及其功能和使用体验

不同观点：
• **Dired模式的优点**：
  - **批量操作和灵活性**：[susam] 强调Dired模式可以轻松标记、操作多个文件，进行批量复制、移动、删除、更改权限等操作，且操作流畅、直观，比标准Unix命令行工具更加方便。
  - **跨环境一致性**：[susam] 指出Dired模式的肌肉记忆和命令在不同系统（如macOS、Xfce4、KDE等）上具有一致性，无论本地还是远程登录，操作体验不变。
  - **脚本化与可记录性**：[susam] 提到Dired的所有操作都可以通过Elisp脚本化，或者通过键盘宏录制和重放，极大提升了自动化操作的可能性。

• **wdired模式的优点**：
  - **可编辑的Dired缓冲区**：[julienchastang], [entropie], [shwouchk] 都提到wdired模式，认为其最大亮点是可以直接在缓冲区中编辑文件名和权限，并通过简单的快捷键（如C-c C-c）提交更改，极大简化了批量文件名修改的过程。
  - **与Emacs其他功能的结合**：[shwouchk] 强调可以使用正则替换、多光标、宏等Emacs功能，进一步增强文件名批量编辑的灵活性。

• **Dired模式的局限与改进建议**：
  - **文件浏览体验不佳**：[ww520] 指出Dired模式默认的文件访问命令会在新窗口中打开文件，导致需要频繁关闭窗口，提出通过自定义Emacs配置解决此问题，并分享了自己的init.el配置代码。
  - **多文件名同时编辑的期待**：[90s_dev] 希望Dired-x模式能够支持像VS Code中的多光标一样同时编辑多个文件名，并希望有人能在Windows Explorer或VS Code中实现这一功能。

• **对Emacs万能化的不同看法**：
  - **积极观点**：[ews] 赞赏Emacs和Guix（或NixOS）的结合，认为可以通过简单的代码复制快速实现配置，令人惊叹。
  - **批评观点**：[paulyy_y] 认为将一切功能都塞进Emacs，甚至称其为操作系统的做法有些过头，表现出对Emacs万能化的质疑。

• **传统工具支持者的观点**：
  - **命令行工具的支持**：[SoftTalker] 表示自己习惯使用shell和诸如cp, mv, rm, find, xargs, grep等命令行工具，认为这些工具已经足够，没有使用Dired模式的需求。

补充讨论：
• **跨平台操作的便捷性**：[susam] 强调了Dired模式在不同系统和环境中的一致性操作体验，这对跨平台用户来说是一个重要优势。
• **快捷键与功能扩展**：[julienchastang], [entropie], [shwouchk] 等人提到了快捷键操作和wdired模式下的编辑功能，显示出Dired模式在快捷操作和功能扩展上的潜力。
• **MIME类型名称的细微差别**：[teddyh] 对术语进行了轻微的纠正，指出“MIME Type”现在应称为“Internet Media Type”。

争议焦点：
• **Emacs万能化**：部分用户如[ews]对Emacs的强大功能和扩展性表示赞赏，而[paulyy_y]则认为将所有功能集成到Emacs中有些过度，表现出对这种万能化趋势的质疑。
• **文件浏览的体验问题**：[ww520] 提出的Dired模式下文件浏览的不便问题，以及其通过自定义配置解决此问题的方案，引发了一些对默认操作不便的讨论。

Using Emacs as your file manager in Guix
The Problem
File managers. They manage your files. Some examples are windows explorer, GNOME's Nautilus, or Dolphin for KDE. If you are a real sicko and only use the terminal, you may be familiar with ranger as well.
They are a perceived necessity in modern-day computing with how easy they make moving, copying, and deleting files.
Well, I don't use any of those. It's not from any self-imposed rule, or a sense of superiority,I just simply forgot they exist.
Whenever I need to edit files, I have emacs. Whenever I need to open files, I have emacs. And whenever I need to delete files, well I tend to do that in the command-line. This is just how I have gotten comfortable working with documents and code and it has not brought on any real need for a file manager. My one exception is when I download something from the internet, and click
Show In Folder
. Nothing happens.
Programs on linux use a database called
xdg-mime
to match certain file types to default programs to handle them. On systems like GNOME or KDE, with full-fledged desktop environments, these are set to things that would make sense: images are opened in an image-viewer. Text files are opened in a text editor, and directories are opened in the file manager. This sounds like a lot of unique programs: an image viewer, a text editor,
and
a file manager? This problem of too-many-programs that I made up for myself is easily solved with a single program, emacs!
MIME stands for "Multi-purpose Internet Mail Extensions and looks something like
text/html
or
application/json
. If you do any work on the frontend of the web, you've encountered these!
The "Solution"
I'm sure some of you reading this are rolling your eyes or reciting the well-known "Emacs is a great OS, but …" I use it a lot, though. I already use
dired-mode
to manage my writing  and programming. It's something that is powerful, and comfortable to use. If you are following along and use something else, it is also quite easy to adjust my code here as well.
Ok, with that out of the way let's look at what we actually want to do: xdg-mime needs to connect "Opening a directory" with "opening emacs in
dired-mode
." First, we need the MIME type for directories. A quick search shows that it is called
inode/directory
.
I have no idea why it is called inode/directory, and I couldn't find an explanation. I've learned not to ask questions about these names.
Opening emacs in
dired-mode
is the easy part: if you pass emacs a directory instead of a file, it automatically opens in the appropriate mode. Great! Now we need to tie these two concepts together.
If we were using a non-declarative system, such as Debian, I would suggest doing something like creating a
.desktop
file, running
xdg-mime default emacs-dired.desktop inode/directory
and that would be it. You could theoretically do this on Guix as well. There is a big downside with this strategy, though: the changes you make are not documented anywhere on your system. If you wanted to duplicate your setup on a new laptop, for example, you would have to either note down this change you made or run into it again, hopefully remember your solution, and then reproduce it. Maybe this works for others, but I know myself. I will not remember, I will run into it again, and then I will get frustrated again. That's why we have
guix-home
configuration.
home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type
is a very helpful service in the
guix-home
configuration tool. It allows you to create
xdg-desktop-entry
for each
.desktop
file you would normally need to create, link those to the MIME type of your choice, and that's it. It is also all written down explicitly, so there is no confusion on what steps were taken. Let's look at the most basic example to solve our issue:
(home-environment
(services
(list
(service home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type
(home-xdg-mime-applications-configuration
(default '((inode/directory . emacs-dired.desktop)))
(desktop-entries
(list (xdg-desktop-entry
(file
"emacs-dired"
)
(name
"Emacs Dired as a file manager"
)
(type 'application)
(config
'((exec .
"emacsclient -c -a emacs %u"
)
(mimetype .
"inode/directory"
)))))))))))
If this is nonsense to you, I apologize. I'm definitely not the person who should be teaching you lisp. You should definitely learn it, though!  The configuration language for Guix is called
Guile Scheme
, read up on it.
I use
emacsclient
here because I have emacs always running as a daemon.
-c
tells it to create a new frame, and
-a emacs
tells it to fall-back to a regular emacs session if there is some reason my daemon has stopped running.
And that's it! It works perfectly after a quick
guix home reconfigure
.  To expand, just add a new
xdg-desktop-entry
that runs whatever script you wish, and then tie it to a MIME type in the
default
list.
I considered adding things for image types, text types, etc. This would be useful to do if you used a regular file manager. With emacs tho

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了20世纪著名历史学家克里斯托弗·希尔（Christopher Hill）的生平和学术贡献。希尔以“底层历史”（history from below）的研究方法闻名，尤其关注英国革命期间的阶级斗争和宗教激进思想。他的代表作《世界颠倒：英国革命中的激进思想》（The World Turned Upside Down: Radical Ideas During the English Revolution）探讨了普通民众在革命中的激进思想及其对民主和平等理念的贡献。尽管希尔一生著作等身，但他也因其对历史的决定论解释受到批评。文章还提到迈克尔·布拉迪克（Michael Braddick）的新书《克里斯托弗·希尔：激进历史学家的一生》（Christopher Hill: The Life of a Radical Historian），该书对希尔的学术和政治生活进行了全面解读。希尔以其平等主义和谦逊的个性而著称，他的工作和思想对后世历史学家产生了深远影响。

Books & the Arts

A World Turned Upside Down
Christopher Hill’s history from below.
Christopher Hill’s Revolutions
The radical life and work of the historian.
Peter Linebaugh
and
Marcus Rediker
Share
Copy Link
Facebook
X (Twitter)
Bluesky
Pocket
Email
Ad Policy
Illustration by Joe Ciardiello.
This article appears in the
June 2025 issue
.
Christopher Hill was one of the most prolific and influential historians of the 20th century. He was also the product of two specific eras of political and social change: the Old Left’s communist and working-class movements of the 1930s and ’40s, and the New Left’s liberation and countercultural movements of the 1960s and ’70s.
At the end of the former, in 1940, Hill wrote
The English Revolution 1640
, which provided a class analysis of the bourgeois revolution against feudalism ﻿and charted a lifetime of scholarship ahead. In the middle of the latter, in 1972, Hill published another book on the same period, his most profound and lasting work,
The World Turned Upside Down: Radical Ideas During the English Revolution
. A social and intellectual history of religious radicals who pioneered the modern ideas and practices of democracy and equality, it was also a book that explored a commoners’ “revolution within the revolution” that, although it failed, nonetheless represented a deep origin story for the history of modern radicalism. Both books, inspired by the movements of their time, helped create the breakthrough that we have now come to call “history from below.”
Books in review
Christopher Hill: The Life of a Radical Historian
by
Michael Braddick
Buy this book
Over a career that spanned more than 60 years, Hill wrote 16 more books, dozens of articles, and seven collections of essays. Along the way, he became the leading interpreter of the English Revolution and its broader 17th century. He also covered an extraordinary range of topics, in books from
Economic Problems of the Church: From Archbishop Whitgift to the Long Parliament
(1956), through
Intellectual Origins of the English Revolution
(1965), to
The English Bible and the Seventeenth-Century Revolution
(1993). He offered creative reinterpretations of the writings and thought of John Milton and John Bunyan, linking each as never before to the radicalism of the English Revolution. His breadth of knowledge, his curiosity, his open-­mindedness, his love of literature, his command of chronology, and his respect for the humanity of his subjects—all of this was evident on every page of every book he wrote.
Michael Braddick’s new book,
Christopher Hill: The Life of a Radical Historian
, offers the first full and comprehensive interpretation of his subject’s life, work, and politics. Braddick admits at the outset that the reserved and private Hill “is not an easy subject for a biographer” and that his book is “more an intellectual life than a biography.” Braddick has conducted impressive research in Hill’s papers at Oxford and the thousands of pages of his published work. As a specialist in Hill’s own field, 17th-century England, Braddick brings to the project deep knowledge of the scholarship by both Hill and his critics. His account is shaped by his affiliation with the “revisionists,” led by John Morrill, who over the past 30 years have worked hard to displace Hill as the leading interpreter of the English Revolution, criticizing him for a teleological bias, determinism, anachronism, and his concept of “bourgeois revolution.” But anyone working in this area of history will have prior disagreements given the immense influence that Hill cast upon his particular field and the profession as a whole. In fact, we are hardly impartial ourselves, as Hill inspired our book
The Many-Headed Hydra
, which we dedicated to him and to his wife, Bridget Hill.
Standing at 5-foot-7, Hill had a sturdy physical presence (he’d been a rugby player in his youth) and a mischievous and ready wit that he often used in self-deprecating ways. He once quipped that he had done a “brave and creditable” job training on a light machine gun for service in World War II, adding: “A thousand pities it was on somebody else’s target.” He also had a stammer, a source of his lifelong shyness and reserve, and described himself as “mean,” by which he meant “cheap.” (His use of pencils endlessly sharpened down to an inch or less was a family joke.)
Hill’s most characteristic trait was his easy egalitarian manner. Former Oxford student Ved Mehta noted that Hill “was singular among dons…that all distinctions of degree, rank, and age were repugnant to him. He was devoid of race prejudice of any kind, and so far ahead of his time that he treated women no differently from men, without a hint of condescension.” Hill’s niece, the historian Penelope Corfield, noted that this commitment to equality, formed early in life, drove his turn toward radicalism in the 1930s.

data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种名为Group Query Attention（GQA）的技术，该技术通过共享键和值的投影来减少多头注意力机制中的内存使用。与传统的Multi-Head Attention（MHA）不同，GQA使用较少的键和值头（$N_{kv}$），并将它们共享给多个查询头（$N_h$），从而降低计算成本和内存占用。具体实现中，先将输入序列通过线性变换得到查询、键和值，然后对键和值进行分组共享，以减少缓存大小。GQA在保持模型性能的同时，显著提高了推理速度并降低了内存需求，特别适用于大型模型的部署。Multi-Query Attention（MQA）是GQA的一种极端形式，其中$N_{kv}$为1。
